data.title: I Messed Up My Google PM Vibe Coding Interview
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI角色面试中的"vibe coding"及其相关争议

不同观点：
• [abxyz] 认为，发帖者（OP）在AI角色面试中遇到"vibe coding"是意料之外的，因为发帖者没有准备好展示这项技能，而不是对角色本身涉及编码感到惊讶。这与一般认为的项目经理（PM）面试中的"vibe coding"情境不同。
• [cavisne] 对帖子的真实性提出质疑，认为大科技公司的面试通常结构严密，招聘人员应明确说明评估内容，因此猜测这可能是个虚假帖子。
• [Incipient] 对"vibe coding"的实际工具链表示好奇，并提到目前使用的开发工具（如VSCode的编辑模式）虽然提高效率，但可能影响代码质量和可扩展性。
• [ChrisMarshallNY] 认为谷歌可能在节省成本，通过雇佣一个能处理多项任务的PM来替代单独的PM和开发人员，反映出当前行业趋势。
• [BSOhealth] 指出，科技行业的角色（如PM、UX/设计等）将在未来融合，并怀疑帖子的真实性，认为大科技公司的面试通常足够结构化，不应出现这种意外。
• [Myrmornis] 认为发帖者并没有进行"vibe coding"，而是尝试实现一个代理，并指出"vibe coding"应在代理存在的前提下进行。
• [tra3] 认为即使发帖者在面试中感到失败，面试官应能透过压力看到所展示的技能。
• [jekwoooooe] 对"vibe coding"产生的应用持负面态度，认为这些应用在生产环境中会崩溃。
• [polotics] 提到曾签署保密协议，与此类话题相关。
• [alshival] 建议不要为大科技公司工作，认为这些公司对员工不重视，并分享了自己在教育和医疗行业工作的积极经验。
• [growbell_social] 认为"vibe coding"将成为许多角色的标准，并预测这是未来的趋势。
• [sunaookami] 认为像这样的帖子在Reddit上很常见，质疑其真实性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于帖子真实性和"vibe coding"在AI角色面试中的合理性。
• 对"vibe coding"工具链和实际效果的讨论，反映出对新技术和工作方式的不同看法。
• 对大科技公司招聘实践和工作文化的批评与辩护。
• 不同行业工作经验的比较，强调了在非科技行业工作的优势。
• 对未来工作角色和技能融合的预测和接受程度。

data.title: Show HN: Vibe Kanban – Kanban board to manage your AI coding agents
data.author: louiskw
data.article_summary: Vibe Kanban 是一个用于管理 AI 编码代理的看板工具。它可以帮助用户轻松切换不同编码代理、编排多个代理并行或顺序执行任务、快速审查工作并启动开发服务器，以及集中管理代理配置。安装时需要通过终端运行 `npx vibe-kanban`，并确保已认证编码代理。该项目使用 Rust 和 Node.js 开发，提供详细的文档和支持。用户可以通过 GitHub 提出问题和功能请求，但不建议未经讨论直接提交 PR。项目源码可在遵循 Apache-2.0 许可证下构建和使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编码工具及其在软件开发中的应用和影响

不同观点：
• [隐私和权限问题]
  ◦ [gpm] 指出该工具默认启用分析功能，收集用户的电子邮件和GitHub用户名，并跟踪各种开发活动，质疑这是否应得到用户的明确同意。
  ◦ [iimblack] 对工具要求的权限感到担忧，质疑一个看板工具为何需要访问代码和部署密钥。

• [工具的实用性和扩展性]
  ◦ [swalsh] 分享了自己构建类似工具的经验，指出在规模化时会出现复合误报的问题，并强调需要手动确认模型识别的潜在问题。
  ◦ [oc1] 提议在软件开发中引入类似厨房 brigade 的角色分配系统，以提高效率。

• [AI在编码中的角色]
  ◦ [adastra22] 质疑AI编码代理是否真的在主导世界代码编写的趋势，并对过度抽象化开发过程表示怀疑。
  ◦ [barbazoo] 认为“人类工程师大部分时间用于规划、审查和协调任务”的说法过于宽泛。

• [用户体验和工作流]
  ◦ [lharries] 对工具的协作功能表示兴趣，询问是否会有托管版本以便团队协作，并提出对依赖性PR管理的改进建议。
  ◦ [uxamanda] 分享了使用GitLab的命令行工具“glab”与混合团队协作的经验。

• [工具的长远价值]
  ◦ [helsinki] 认为该工具目前提供的功能终端和Git工作树也能实现，质疑其对高级用户的吸引力。
  ◦ [deepdarkforest] 对过度依赖AI编码代理表示担忧，认为这种抽象化可能会引入噪音和草率，特别是在企业级代码中。

• [生产力和工作满意度]
  ◦ [skeeter2020] 幽默地提出了在使用AI工具极大提升生产力后如何利用空闲时间的问题。
  ◦ [notarobot123] 对长期使用这种工作流的感受表示好奇，询问这种工作方式是否可持续并令人满意。

• [市场竞争和未来发展]
  ◦ [_jayhack_] 认为这种项目对传统项目管理平台构成威胁，并指出像Linear、Monday、ClickUp等平台正在积极改善UX以适应人机协作。

补充讨论：
• [工具推荐和资源整合]
  ◦ [mahsima] 建议将该工具添加到相关的AI编码工具列表中，以便更多人发现和使用。

争议焦点：
• 该工具的隐私问题和权限要求是否合理。
• AI编码代理在软件开发中的角色和影响，特别是对代码质量和开发过程的影响。
• 该工具是否提供了足够的独特功能以吸引高级用户和企业用户。

Get 10X more out of Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Amp and other coding agents...
Overview
AI coding agents are increasingly writing the world's code and human engineers now spend the majority of their time planning, reviewing, and orchestrating tasks. Vibe Kanban streamlines this process, enabling you to:
Easily switch between different coding agents
Orchestrate the execution of multiple coding agents in parallel or in sequence
Quickly review work and start dev servers
Track the status of tasks that your coding agents are working on
Centralise configuration of coding agent MCP configs
You can watch a video overview
here
.
Installation
Make sure you have authenticated with your favourite coding agent. A full list of supported coding agents can be found in the
docs
. Then in your terminal run:
npx vibe-kanban
Documentation
Please head to the
website
for the latest documentation and user guides.
Support
Please open an issue on this repo if you find any bugs or have any feature requests.
Contributing
We would prefer that ideas and changes are raised with the core team via GitHub issues, where we can discuss implementation details and alignment with the existing roadmap. Please do not open PRs without first discussing your proposal with the team.
Development
Prerequisites
Rust
(latest stable)
Node.js
(>=18)
pnpm
(>=8)
pnpm i
Running the dev server
pnpm run dev
This will start the frontend and backend with live reloading. A blank DB will be copied from the
dev_assets_seed
folder.
Build from source
Run
build-npm-package.sh
In the
npx-cli
folder run
npm pack
You can run your build with
npx [GENERATED FILE].tgz

data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文研究了极轻强度运动对静息状态下自发眨眼率（rssEBR）和执行功能的影响。24名健康年轻人参与了10分钟的极轻强度骑自行车运动和休息对照实验。结果显示，运动后眨眼率没有显著变化，但眨眼率的变化与斯特鲁普任务表现的改善存在显著相关性。这表明，虽然极轻强度运动不会一致增加眨眼率，但运动引发的眨眼率变化可以预测个体执行功能的增强程度。因此，rssEBR可能作为预测运动对大脑健康和认知影响的非侵入性生物标志物。

Abstract
Background
Acute physical exercise, even at a very-light-intensity, potentiates prefrontal cortex activation and improves executive function. The underlying circuit mechanisms in the brain remain poorly understood, though we speculate a potential involvement of arousal-related neuromodulatory systems. Recently, our rodent study demonstrated that exercise, even at light-intensity, activates the midbrain dopaminergic neurons. Resting-state spontaneous eye blink rate is linked to brain-arousal neural circuits, and potentially to those modulated by dopaminergic system. We hypothesized that neural substrates linked to resting-state eye blink rate contribute to the cognitive impact of acute very-light-intensity exercise.
Method
We analyzed data from a previous study with a renewed focus on resting-state eye blink rate. Twenty-four healthy young adults completed both 10 min of cycling (very-light-intensity exercise: 30% peak oxygen uptake) and rest conditions. Resting-state eye blink rate and Stroop task performance were measured before and after both exercise and resting control.
Results
Results showed no significant differences in eye blink rate changes between conditions. However, correlation analyses revealed that exercise-induced changes in resting-state eye blink rate were significantly associated with individual variations in Stroop task performance enhancement.
Conclusion
Very-light-intensity exercise does not elicit a consistent increase in eye blink rate after exercise. This finding does not support the involvement of a blink increase-linked neural substrate in enhancing executive function through very-light-intensity exercise. However, resting-state eye blink rate that is altered by exercise is predictive of executive function enhancement levels; this may serve as a novel contactless biomarker for predicting exercise benefits for brain health and cognition.

data.author: type0
data.article_summary: 文章主要报道了欧洲情报机构指控俄罗斯在乌克兰广泛使用违禁化学武器，包括氯气和氯化苦（一种可致命的化学剂），以迫使乌军出洞并进行攻击。德国和荷兰情报机构指出，俄方的这种行为违反了《化学武器公约》。乌克兰及其支持者呼吁对俄实施更严厉制裁，并限制其参与国际组织。俄罗斯否认指控，反称乌克兰使用化学武器。此前，美国也曾指责俄方使用化学武器，但双方的指控均未得到充分证实。乌克兰方面报告了数千起与化学武器相关的伤害事件，局势令人担忧。

Dutch intelligence said the chemical is dropped from Russian drones to force soldiers out of trenches so they can be shot, as Russia looks to continue making gains on the battlefield despite international efforts towards peace.
The chemical, which was widely used during World War One, can cause irritation of the lungs, eyes and skin and can cause diarrhoea, vomiting and nausea.

"The main conclusion is that we can confirm Russia is intensifying its use of chemical weapons," Dutch defence minister Ruben Brekelmans told Reuters, as he called for tougher sanctions for Moscow.
"This intensification is concerning because it is part of a trend we have been observing for several years now, where Russia's use of chemical weapons in this war is becoming more normalized, standardized, and widespread."
Germany’s BND foreign intelligence agency said Russia has been using not only tear gas but also "the more dangerous chemical chloropicrin, which can be lethal in high concentrations in enclosed spaces". This is a more serious violation of the Chemical Weapons Convention, it added.
European intelligence officials fear that Russia’s chemical weapons use is part of a large-scale intensification of chemical weapons production, and that Russian officials are issuing direct instructions to soldiers to use the poisonous warfare agents.
Russian chemical weapons use is “truly part of a large scale programme” rather than “some ad-hoc tinkering at the frontline”, said Peter Reesink, the head of the Dutch military intelligence agency (MIVD).

The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), a disarmament agency in The Hague with 193 member states, said last year that initial accusations levelled by both countries at each other were "insufficiently substantiated".

data.title: Repasting a MacBook
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者试图为四年前的M1 Pro MacBook Pro更换导热膏以解决风扇噪音问题，但遭遇了一系列意外。起初，作者发现旧的导热膏已经干涸，计划用新的导热膏替换。然而，在拆解过程中，不小心弄坏了风扇电缆，之后又意外损坏了Touch ID传感器的电缆。文章解释了导热膏的作用和其随时间干涸的问题，并详细描述了拆解过程中的困难。最终，由于Touch ID传感器的加密配对特性，作者无法简单更换电缆，导致维修失败。作者建议普通用户不要轻易尝试自行更换MacBook的导热膏，以免造成不可逆的损坏。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MacBook散热改造及维修难度

不同观点：
• [zdw] 提出在没有风扇的MacBook型号上，可以通过在CPU散热器和外壳之间添加导热垫，将整个底壳变成一个大散热片，从而延长最大性能时间。缺点是外壳会变得很热，但可以通过加装硬壳保护套解决。

• [t1234s] 分享了个人经验，提到2012年的MBP易于拆卸和维修，而2017年的MBP则质量和维修难度都很差。同时质疑新款M3/M4 MBP是否在拆卸和换电池方面有所改善。

• [dclowd9901] 将散热改造后的感觉比作给汽车换油，认为虽然实际变化不大，但主观感觉设备变得更健康。

• [gruez] 警告称，使用普通PC导热膏可能会在几个月后导致性能下降，因为它们比笔记本专用的导热材料更容易“泵出”。

• [haiku2077] 强调不应在Mac上使用普通导热膏或导热垫，建议使用专门的TCRS Carbon Black，而不是更换新零件。

• [gdbsjjdn] 对“友好拆卸过程”与“高昂维修成本”之间的矛盾表示讽刺。

• [smallpipe] 对比ThinkPad和MacBook的维修难度，认为MacBook虽然性能好但维修性差。

• [moribvndvs] 认为笔记本不适合长期高CPU使用，建议使用台式机进行此类工作。

• [nottorp] 表示旧款MacBook更具可玩性，并分享了个人的旧款MacBook改造经历。

• [jeron] 认为文章更像是在劝阻用户不要重新涂抹导热膏，质疑5度的降温和100分的Cinebench提升是否值得。

• [dsego] 分享了最近清洁MacBook的经历，指出灰尘导致的风扇噪音问题，并计划更换电池和扬声器。

• [ksec] 质疑为何笔记本不默认使用PCM（相变材料）作为导热介质，认为成本增加有限。

• [pram] 提到当前MBP的风扇几乎不运转，且内部几乎没有灰尘。

• [dmsnell] 分享了自己多次更换导热膏的经验，并指出导热膏降解对设备性能的长期影响。

补充讨论：
- 维修难度和设备设计变化是多个评论者关注的焦点，尤其是旧款和新款MacBook的对比。
- 导热材料的选择和使用寿命是另一个值得注意的讨论点，不同用户对导热膏的效果和风险有不同看法。
- 主观感受与客观性能变化之间的差异在评论中也得到了体现。

44531569.article_content:
You should repaste your MacBook (but don't)
July 10, 2025
My favorite memory of my M1 Pro MacBook Pro was the whole sensation of “holy crap, you
never
hear the fans in this thing”, which was very novel in 2021.
Four years later, this MacBook Pro is still a delight. It’s the longest I’ve ever owned a laptop, and while I’d love to pick up the new M4 goodness, this dang thing still seems to just shrug at basically anything I throw at it. Video editing, code compiling, CAD models, the works. (My desire to update
is
helped though by the fact I got the 2TB SSD, 32GB RAM option, and upgrading to those on new MacBooks is still eye wateringly expensive.)
But my MacBook is starting to show its age in one area: it’s not quiet anymore.
If you’re doing anything too intensive like compiling code for awhile, or converting something in Handbrake, the age of the fans being quiet is long past. The fans are properly loud. (And despite having two cats, it’s not them! I clean out the fans pretty regularly.)
Enter the thermal paste
Everyone online seems to point toward one thing: the thermal paste on computers tends to dry up over the years.
What the heck is thermal paste? Well, components on your computer that generate a lot of heat are normally made to touch something like a copper heatsink that is really good at
pulling
that heat away from it. The issue is, when you press these two metal surfaces against each other, even the best machining isn’t perfect and you there’s microscopic gaps between them meaning there’s just air at those parts, and air is a terrible conductor of heat.
The solution is to put a little bit of thermal paste (basically a special grey toothpaste gunk that is really good at transferring heat) between them, and it fills in any of those microscopic gaps.
The problem with this solution is after hundreds and hundreds of days of intense heat, the paste can dry up into something closer to almost a powder, and it’s not nearly as good at filling in those gaps.
Replacement time
The logic board!
MacBook thermal paste isn’t anything crazy (for the most part, see below), custom PC builders use thermal paste all the time so incredibly performant options are available online. I grabbed a tube of Noctua NT-H2 for about $10 and set to taking apart my MacBook to swap out the aging thermal paste. And thankfully,
iFixit has a tremendous, in depth guide
on the disassembly required, so I got to it.
Indeed, that grey thermal paste looked quite old, but also above and below it (on the RAM chips) I noticed something that didn’t quite seem like thermal paste, it was far moreâ¦ grainy almost?
Spottiness is due to half of it being on the heatsink
It turns out, ending with my generation of MacBooks (lucky me!) Apple used a very special kind of thermal compound often called “
Carbon Black
”, which is basically designed to be able to bridge an even thicker gap than traditional thermal paste. I thought about replacing it, but it seems really hard to come across that special thermal compound (and do not do it with normal thermal paste) and my RAM temperatures always seemed fine (65Â°C is fineâ¦ right?) so I just made sure to not touch that.
For the regular grey thermal paste, I used some cotton swabs and isopropyl alcohol to remove the dried up existing thermal paste, then painted on a bit of the new stuff.
Disaster
To get to the underside of the CPU, you basically need to disassemble the entire MacBook. It’s honestly not that hard, but iFixit warned that the fan cables (which also need to be unclipped) are incredibly delicate. And they’re not wrong, seriously they have the structural integrity of the half-ply toilet paper available at gas stations.
So, wouldn’t you know it, I moved the left fan’s cable a bit too hard and it completely tore in half. Gah.
I found a replacement fan online (yeah you can’t just buy the cable, need a whole new fan) and in the meantime I just kept an eye on my CPU thermals. As long as I wasn’t doing anything too intensive it honestly always stayed around 65Â° which was warm, but not terrifying (MacBook Airs completely lack a fan, after all).
Take two
A few days later, the fans arrived, and I basically had to redo the entire disassembly process to get to the fans. At least I was a lot faster this time.
The fan was incredibly easy to swap out (hats off there, Apple!) and I screwed everything back together and began reconnecting all the little connectors.
Until I saw it: the tiny (made of the same half ply material as the fan cable) Touch ID sensor cable was inexpicably torn in half, the top half just hanging out. I didn’t even touch this thing really, and I hadn’t even got to the stage of reconnecting it (I was about to!), it comes from underneath the logic board and I guess just the movement of sliding the logic board back in sheared it in half.
me
Bah. I looked up if I could just grab another replacement cable here, and sure enough you canâ¦ but the Touch ID chip is cryptographically paired to your MacBook

data.title: The great Malaysian cooking oil arbitrage
data.author: valkrieco
data.article_summary: 马来西亚的烹饪油补贴和欧盟的生物燃料 mandate 创造了一个套利机会：新鲜油可以低价购买、重新标记为“使用过的”油，然后高价卖给航空燃料生产商。根据《海峡时报》和《气候之家新闻》的报道，马来西亚马六甲出现了一个 scheme，当地人将烹饪油卖给那些供应欧洲航空燃料生产商的中介。欧盟要求航空公司使用更多来自可持续来源的生物燃料，而马来西亚政府补贴烹饪油，使得购买新鲜油便宜，转售“使用过的”油则有利可图。餐馆可以合法地通过使用几次后卖掉废油获利，但有人直接购买新鲜油而不使用，谎称是“使用过的”油，以赚取差价。这种欺诈行为动机明显且机会充足，马来西亚收集的“使用过的”油量惊人，人均远超其他国家。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44543781.article_content:
Malaysian cooking oil subsidies and EU biofuel mandates have
created
an arbitrage opportunity where fresh oil can be bought cheap, relabelled as 'used', and sold at a profit to aviation fuel producers.
...the Straits Times and Climate Home News recently reported on a striking scheme in Melaka, Malaysia, where locals were selling cooking oil that would eventually be used to supply European producers of aviation fuel.
The underlying idea of turning a waste product, used cooking oil, into something that can be blended into aviation fuel seems as appealing as
getting the cobras out of Delhi
. Cooking oil starts tasting bad after being used for frying three to five times, but as an input to aviation fuel, used oil is perfectly good.
At this point two intriguing forces intersect: European governments are demanding that airlines use more biofuels from sustainable sources — used cooking oil being one — while the Malaysian government subsidises cooking oil.
This means that in Malaysia buying fresh oil is cheap and selling used oil is lucrative. If you run a food stall or restaurant in Malaysia, you can buy subsidised fresh oil, fry food a few times, then sell the waste oil at a profit. It’s a nice side-hustle.
The trouble is, writes financial journalist Matt Levine, “If you don’t run a restaurant, you can buy fresh cooking oil for $0.60, not use it to fry food any times, and then say, ‘Oh, yeah we totally used this oil,’ and sell it to a refiner for $1.” That seems a simpler and more scalable way to proceed. It certainly cuts out the precarious, time-consuming hassle of actually running a restaurant. It is hard to know how much fresh oil is being resold this way, but fraudsters have both the motive and the opportunity.
Climate Home news notes that Malaysia collects an astonishing volume of “used” cooking oil: more per person than anywhere else, and two and a half times as much as second-placed Singapore.

data.title: Upgrading an M4 Pro Mac mini's storage for half the price
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者通过DIY升级套件将M4 Pro Mac mini的存储从512GB升级到4TB的过程。升级使用了M4-SSD提供的产品，总成本为699美元，远低于苹果官方的1200美元升级价格。升级过程相对简单，但需要小心拆卸后盖以避免损坏。由于采用 proprietary 接口，升级后必须通过DFU模式恢复系统。性能测试显示，升级后的内部存储在写入速度上优于外部Thunderbolt SSD，且更为稳定。尽管升级费用较高，但相比苹果官方选项仍具性价比。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple SSD的性能、可升级性、价格以及数据完整性等问题。

不同观点：
• [dylan604] 认为SSD的速度非常惊人，相比过去的机械硬盘（HDD）阵列有显著提升，尤其是在视频编辑等实际应用中表现出色。他还提到过去需要多个设备和繁琐的操作才能达到现在的性能，而现在的SSD技术让工作流程更加高效。

• [GeekyBear] 指出Apple将SSD控制器集成到SOC（系统级芯片）中的一个重要原因可能是数据完整性。通过引用Apple收购Anobit的案例，说明Apple在NAND闪存的可靠性和寿命方面做了大量技术投资，以提升数据保存的稳定性。

• [Andrew_nenakhov] 批评Apple产品的存储和内存不可升级，并指出Apple对存储和内存的定价过高，例如32GB RAM/1TB版本的价格是16GB RAM/512GB版本的两倍，认为这种定价策略不合理。

• [radley] 分享了购买SSD后因过热问题而需要更换的经历，并提到卖家不提供保修，这使得购买高价SSD存在一定风险。

• [yread] 强烈批评Apple的4TB SSD价格过高，认为这是不合理的溢价。

• [dewey] 支持DIY升级，认为通过自行升级可以大幅节省成本，并且操作相对简单、可逆，性价比高。

• [gandalfian] 提到Apple产品的硬件限制（如5400rpm硬盘）对性能的影响，并通过自行更换NVMe SSD显著提升了设备性能，但也对Apple的产品设计表示不满。

• [Zenst] 讨论了可更换存储和焊接升级之间的差异，认为可更换存储更安全，而焊接升级的风险较高，需要专业技术。

• [zwilliamson] 提出使用其他品牌和操作系统（如Beelink SER8和Arch Linux + Wayland）作为Apple产品的替代方案，认为这样可以大幅节省成本并获得更高的可定制性。

• [gpm] 认为外部SSD在性价比和灵活性方面更具优势，特别是在不需要极高速度的场景下，外部SSD是更好的选择。

• [porphyra] 提到中国的一些店铺提供Mac mini的SSD升级服务，价格更便宜且包括DFU恢复等操作。

• [wpm] 强烈批评Apple在存储和内存方面的定价策略，认为这是不合理的“抢劫”，并指出Apple过去允许用户自行升级硬件，而现在则通过硬件限制和过高定价迫使消费者支付额外费用。

• [bee_rider] 对Apple产品命名中的“M”系列芯片名称提出疑问，认为命名不够清晰，容易引起混淆。

• [ProllyInfamous] 分享了自己使用四个4TB SATA驱动器和Terramaster外部硬盘盒构建16TB外部SSD RAID0的经历，认为这种DIY方案在性价比上优于购买Apple的高价SSD。

• [gigatexal] 认为为了节省时间和精力，直接支付Apple的“税”是值得的，因为时间比金钱更宝贵。

补充讨论：
1. 争议焦点主要集中在Apple SSD的高价和不可升级性上，部分用户认为这是不合理的定价策略，而另一些用户则认为可以通过DIY升级或外部SSD来解决。
2. 数据完整性和性能也是讨论的重要方面，尤其是Apple通过技术投资提升SSD可靠性的努力得到了部分用户的认可。
3. 不同用户对Apple产品设计和定价的满意度存在明显差异，一些用户强烈不满，而另一些用户则愿意支付额外费用以获得便利和性能提升。

44532306.article_content:
Upgrading an M4 Pro Mac mini's storage for half the price
A few months ago, I
upgraded my M4 Mac mini from 1 to 2 TB of internal storage
, using a then-$269 DIY upgrade kit from ExpandMacMini.
At the time, there was no option for upgrading the M4 Pro Mac mini, despite it
also
using a
user-replaceable
, socketed storage drive.
But the folks at
M4-SSD
reached out and asked if I'd be willing to test out one of their new M4 Pro upgrades, in this case, upgrading the mini I use at the studio for editing from a stock 512 GB SSD to
4 TB
.
I said yes, and here we are!
I documented the entire upgrade—along with taking my old M4 mini 1TB SSD and putting it in my
Dad's
M4 mini—in today's video:
But please continue reading, if you prefer text over video, like I do :)
The
upgrade process
itself is straightforward (if you've ever worked on laptop hardware before, at least), though removing the rear plastic cover (which also has the power button attached) is a bit annoying.
There are four metal pegs that are retained in clips in the bottom metal cover, and you have to slide a thin piece of metal / pry tool into the very minimal gap between the plastic bottom cover and the aluminum case, then pry it up. And if you're not careful on that step, you'll not only scratch the aluminum (and maybe crack the plastic bottom), but there's a good chance you rip the fragile (and tiny) power button connector too!
Besides that, it's a matter of removing a number of small torx screws; all the bits I needed were present in the cheapest iFixit assortment I have at my desk.
The only substantial difference between the M4 and M4 Pro mini SSD is the size and relative location—the M4 Pro has a much longer slot, a little more than a standard 2242-size NVMe SSD, while the M4 has a shorter slot, closer to a 2230.
DFU Restore
Speaking of standards... you
have
to do a full DFU (Device Firmware Update) restore, because unlike conventional M.2 NVMe storage, the M4 uses a proprietary connector, a proprietary-sized slot, and splits up the typical layout—the card that's user-replaceable is actually just flash chips and supporting power circuits, while the storage controller (the NVMe 'brains') is part of the M4 SoC (System on a Chip). Apple could use standard NVMe slots, but they seem to think the controller being part of the SoC brings better security... it certainly doesn't bring any cost savings, resiliency in terms of quick recovery from failure in the field, or performance advantage!
Since DFU restore is necessary, in my earlier video, I suggested you need an Apple Silicon mac (M1 or later) as the other computer.
But I was corrected by my viewers, who mentioned you can use many Intel Macs as well—I believe as long as a T2 chip is present, you're good to go. Just connect to the
middle
Thunderbolt port on the rear of the Mac mini, then press and hold the power button while plugging it into AC power. The other Mac should pop up an 'Allow this device to connect?' dialog and then you can proceed to the
DFU process
from there.
As far as I'm aware, no Hackintosh or other computer can be made to do a DFU restore.
I've done three upgrades (two on M4 minis, one on an M4 Pro mini), and all three were easy. The second one, I thought I had an issue, but it was just a confirmation dialog that wound up
behind
the active window.
Performance
I decided to also use an external Thunderbolt 5 NVMe enclosure from M4-SSD along with my (rather expensive) 8TB Sabrent Rocket Q SSD, and do a performance comparison.
See the video at the beginning of this post for some more detail (like all the numbers from
AmorphousDiskMark
and
Blackmagic Disk Speed Test
), but here are the raw numbers for large file copy performance:
The upgraded 4TB module performed noticeably better in writes, likely because it has more flash chips on it to spread out the write activity. Reads were pretty close to the same, with minor variance in performance across different file sizes and access patterns.
The external TB5 drive was the laggard, but is still ridiculously fast (by my standards, editing 4K video). And it would likely be faster if I used a good PCIe Gen 4x4 drive (the Rocket Q is Gen 3x4).
But the internal storage on these Mac minis is very fast, and even better, very
consistently
fast. The external Thunderbolt drive would slow down briefly every minute or so, after 100+ GB were copied—and I verified both with
smartctl
and
my thermal camera
that the drive was not overheating.
This is likely due to the internal DRAM cache on the NVMe SSD not being able to keep up with the high transfer speeds over long periods of time.
Conclusion
I was provided the
$699 M4 Pro 4TB SSD upgrade
by M4-SSD. It's quite expensive (especially compared to
normal
4TB NVMe SSDs, which range from $200-400)...
But it's not nearly as expensive as Apple's own offering, which at the time of this writing is
$1,200
!
Further reading
Don't pay $800 for Apple's 2TB SSD upgrade

• [ProllyInfamous] 分享了自己使用四个4TB SATA驱动器和Terramaster外部硬盘盒构建16TB外部SSD RAID0的经历，认为这种DIY方案在性价比上优于购买Apple的高价SSD。

• [gigatexal] 认为为了节省时间和精力，直接支付Apple的“税”是值得的，因为时间比金钱更宝贵。

补充讨论：
1. 争议焦点主要集中在Apple SSD的高价和不可升级性上，部分用户认为这是不合理的定价策略，而另一些用户则认为可以通过DIY升级或外部SSD来解决。
2. 数据完整性和性能也是讨论的重要方面，尤其是Apple通过技术投资提升SSD可靠性的努力得到了部分用户的认可。
3. 不同用户对Apple产品设计和定价的满意度存在明显差异，一些用户强烈不满，而另一些用户则愿意支付额外费用以获得便利和性能提升。

data.article_summary: 2025年6月，太阳能首次成为欧盟最大的电力来源，提供了创纪录的22%电力。根据智库Ember的分析，至少13个国家太阳能发电量创下新高，荷兰和希腊的太阳能发电占比分别超过40%和35%。核能是第二大电力来源，随后是风能、天然气和水电。煤炭发电仅占6%，创下新低，15个欧盟国家已无煤电。6月的热浪期间，太阳能帮助缓解了电网压力，避免了停电。气候变化加剧了高温，导致大量与高温相关的死亡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲可再生能源，特别是太阳能的发展及其面临的挑战

不同观点：
• [mrtksn]: 对太阳能技术感到兴奋，认为欧洲由于缺乏化石燃料，发展绿色能源并非选择而是必要。虽然不反对核能，但认为其建设周期过长。还设想了一个全自动的太阳能光伏板工厂，可以自行扩展并利用捕获的太阳能生产面板。

• [ricardo81]: 指出太阳能和风能的平准化发电成本（LCOE）最低，但由于公众缺乏认知以及政治信仰的分歧，这一事实并未普及。认为国家应奖励已经采用绿色能源的人，而不是支付边际价格。

• [Someone]: 强调文章标题用词不准确，指出太阳能只是在电力供应中占比最大，而不是整个能源供应中占比最大。

• [toomuchtodo]: 认为需要更多的储能技术来稳定可再生能源的波动。欧洲电网目前依赖于天然气、法国核能和挪威水电来平衡可再生能源的波动。

• [ethan_smith]: 指出太阳能尽管容量因子较低（约15-25%），但依然达到了 headline 所描述的成绩，这意味着安装容量可能是 headline 数字的3-4倍。

• [layer8]: 提到西欧经历了有记录以来最热的六月，这一气候现象可能与太阳能发电量的增加有关。

• [exiguus]: 提到德国的可再生能源占比约70%，并计划在2035年前淘汰化石能源，最后一座核电站已于2023年关闭。

• [bryanlarsen]: 认为这一结果是经过挑选的，不像加州那样全面，但仍是一个好的进展。

• [athenot]: 指出六七月太阳能发电量高是合理的，但在十二月情况会有所不同。认为多样化的能源生产是好事，没有单一的解决方案，太阳能、风能、核能、化石能源和水电都有其优缺点。

• [Theodores]: 认为欧洲缺乏本土能源，长期依赖进口石油、天然气、铀和煤炭。指出可再生能源的崛起部分是由于制造业外迁，且很多太阳能技术来自中国，欧洲并非技术领先者。还提到乌克兰危机后欧洲对能源安全的担忧。

• [dexterdog]: 认为标题应明确为电网电力，并质疑柴油仍是所有能源发电中的主要来源。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及太阳能技术的潜力和限制，如其低容量因子、储能问题及与其他能源的互补性。
• 政治和经济因素对可再生能源发展的影响，如公众认知、政策奖励及能源独立性。
• 不同国家（如德国和英国）在可再生能源转型中的具体策略和进展。
• 全球化对欧洲能源和制造业的影响，以及对能源安全的担忧。

44533843.article_content:
E360 Digest
July 11, 2025
In a First, Solar Was Europe’s Biggest Source of Power Last Month
Solar panels in Zaragoza, Spain.
Fernando Tomás via Flickr
For the first time, solar was the largest source of electricity in the EU last month, supplying a record 22 percent of the bloc’s power.
At least 13 countries saw solar output hit a new monthly high in June, according to an
analysis
from energy think tank Ember. Solar amounted to more than 40 percent of generation in the Netherlands and 35 percent in Greece.
Nuclear was the second biggest source of electricity across the bloc, followed by wind, natural gas, and hydropower. Coal generated just 6 percent of electricity, a new monthly low. Fifteen EU countries are now coal-free, including Austria, Belgium, and Ireland, which
shuttered
its last coal plant last month.
Analysts say that the June surge in solar power
helped
Europe weather a brutal heat wave, which saw
temperatures
soar upwards of 110 degrees F (43 degrees C). Solar power was most abundant at midday, when there was the greatest demand for air conditioning, helping to ease strain on the grid and prevent blackouts.
“Heat waves will not go away – they will only get more severe in the future,” said Pawel Czyzak, an analyst at Ember. “Luckily, there is no lack of sunshine during heat waves.”
Last month was the
warmest
June on record in Europe, and scientists say that climate change played a key role in the heat wave, pushing temperatures to dangerous extremes. An
analysis
from Imperial College London found that warming was responsible for 1,500 of the estimated 2,300 heat-related deaths across Europe, meaning “the death toll was tripled due to the burning of fossil fuels.”

data.title: I'm done with social media – Or: why I have a blog now
data.author: anarbadalov
data.article_summary: 作者原本计划在2024年通过社交媒体积极推广自己的新书《A Body Made of Glass》，以增加成功的机会。这本书因体裁不易分类、主题个人化且作者并非该领域的知名专家，使得推广更加困难。作者参加培训、请教专业人士，并专注于Instagram和TikTok，制作大量视频，分享每一个小成就。然而，作者很快感到不适，不擅长面对镜头，视频制作耗时，且这种方式开始改变其对生活的看法，使其生活变得像为了拍摄而存在。最终，作者对这种自我推广方式产生厌恶，特别是当发现这些努力并未得到社交媒体算法的青睐时，感到沮丧并决定放弃。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体的使用、其对个人生活和工作的影响、以及未来发展趋势

不同观点：
• stego-tech认为，当前技术行业的过度集中和消费端缺乏创新使得人们开始重新审视自己与技术的关系，更多人会选择根据自己的价值观做出决策，尽管这可能会导致一些冲突。这种趋势可能会促使更多人选择脱离某些技术产品，而不是全面反对技术本身。
• teekert指出，大型社交媒体平台（如Facebook）存在不尊重用户的行为，例如通过误导性邮件诱导用户重新登录，这种行为让人感到不适。
• kmarc认为，社交媒体上的“创作者”和“消费者”有不同的体验，创作者容易迷失在追求关注和模仿他人的过程中，而观看者则可能沉迷于这些内容，失去其他更有意义的活动时间。
• freeopinion强调，社交媒体的初衷是促进人与人之间的交流，例如分享个人生活动态。然而，大多数人将社交媒体平台用作新闻或娱乐服务，而非纯粹的社交工具。此外，优质的社交媒体服务可能需要收费，但不确定有多少人愿意为此付费。
• mattgreenrocks将社交媒体比作大型多人在线游戏，目标是积累关注和社交指标，而非真正解决问题或创造价值。他认为，社交媒体提供的是真实沟通和行动的苍白影子，人们应该追求更多真实的生活体验。
• mrtksn怀念早期的互联网，认为当前的互联网被盈利性内容和算法主导，但相信未来会有新的形式出现，使得非极端主义的高质量内容再次繁荣。
• shortn提倡使用RSS feeds来替代社交媒体平台的算法控制，认为这样可以更好地管理内容消费，并减少不必要的精神负担。
• TechDebtDevin分享了自己因在Instagram上看到暴力内容而产生的焦虑经历，决定暂时退出社交媒体，转向Mastodon和Signal等更安全的平台。
• anarbadalov指出，社交媒体并非推广书籍的可靠工具，许多作者在此方面未能成功，且社交媒体的剥削性动态使得作者更难从中受益。
• alexpotato为社交媒体辩护，认为尽管其有诸多缺点，但在职业网络和行业交流中仍然具有重要作用，特别是对于寻找相关社区和分享个人见解的人来说。
• techterrier选择放弃Instagram，转而创建个人网站来展示自己的爱好作品，尽管访问量不高，但感到满意。
• tiniuclx尝试用社交媒体推广音乐和应用多年未果，感觉平台上的算法内容淹没了真实的社交互动。
• game_the0ry假设，媒体制作将从社交媒体平台逐渐转向个人化（去中心化）平台，因为用户对平台及其算法的疲劳感和不信任感增加，创作者也面临平台的限制和货币化困难。

补充讨论：
• 社交媒体的初衷和当前使用方式的偏离：许多人将社交媒体用作新闻和娱乐工具，而非纯粹的社交工具。
• 平台算法对用户体验的影响：算法推送导致用户看到大量噪音和煽动性内容，用户对此感到疲劳。
• 创作者在社交媒体平台上面临的挑战：包括难以货币化和随时可能被封禁的风险。
• 未来互联网和社交媒体的发展趋势：一些人认为去中心化平台和个人网站将逐渐取代当前的大型社交媒体平台。

争议焦点：
• 社交媒体的价值和危害：一些人认为社交媒体提供了重要的职业和社交机会，而另一些人则强调其带来的精神负担和负面影响。
• 去中心化平台是否会取代当前的社交媒体巨头：一些人看好去中心化趋势，而另一些人则未明确表态。

44532913.article_content:
I started last year with one clear goal: 2024 was going to be the year that I finally
did
social media. Regular posting, a content calendar, a strategy, a plan for growth — all of that. And yet I ended the year pretty certain that I never wanted to open those apps again, let alone post my photos and words to them. How?
My main motivation for wanting to conquer my long-held ambivalence about posting was because I had
a book
coming out in April 2024. I was very anxious about this, in part because
A Body Made of Glass
was not an obviously easy sell. There are a few reasons for that: it blends several genres in a hard-to-categorise way, it tackles a subject in which I am not a well-known or previously published expert, and it is highly personal. It had also, in quite a modest way, done well according to the nebulous pre-publication benchmarks that authors obsess over. It had attracted a "Big Five" publisher in the US, something I had not had before, received a BBC radio serialisation deal in the UK, and had received some decent early reviews from industry publications in both places. I felt I should be leaving no stone unturned to support the book's success, since I had been gifted opportunities that many other writers would love to have. Chances, too, that I may never have again.
There are very few things that an author can practically do to make a book a success, especially after said book is written, edited and printed. Being a celebrity or personality with a pre-existing audience that adores you definitely helps, but isn't something you can suddenly decide to become four months before your publication date. Catching a particular trend or moment that causes publishers to invest heavily in promotion and booksellers to place large early orders is great too, but once the book is done that's up to them, not you. Giving off that nebulous aura of "I'm about to become a huge literary success" that seems to cling to some people and not others would be good as well, but is also pretty hard to engineer deliberately if that's not your personality or presentation (and it isn't mine).
In that tense, quiet period after the book has been finalised but before anyone can buy or read it, augmenting your personal brand via the regular use of social media feels like the only concrete action you can take. Or at least it did to me, so I threw myself into it. I attended some training sessions on "social media for authors". I asked professional acquaintances with expertise for tips. I learned that Instagram and TikTok were the best platforms to target for bookish followers and that the algorithms of these platforms were, these days, only interested in vertical videos. I compiled lists of videos I could make and started filming mostly-daily updates about my experience as an author with a book coming out soon. I scoured the accounts of other authors who were more successful than me on social media for insights. I posted about every tiny bit of publicity my book got or small win I achieved. I asked people to pre-order in as many ways as I could think of. I delved into the analytics, searching for ways to optimise and improve. I spent a lot of time scrolling, and scrolling, and scrolling, hunting for the "one weird trick" that would help me make a success of this.
I quickly began to feel quite uncomfortable. I'm not a natural on camera and I don't have that talent for talking effortlessly and engagingly to a lens when alone in a room that successful social media personalities need. I was forcing it all the time, making myself record multiple takes and doing things again and again until they looked "natural" (a highly unnatural behaviour). My video editing skills are basic, so turning out regular videos took me a long time. Worst of all, though, was the way in which this enterprise began to alter my mindset about the normal stuff of life. I never used to think very hard about what I wore for a casual day of writing at home, or worry about how clean the bathroom mirror was, or obsess over what narrative or story might emerge from my general jumble of accumulated tasks. It shocked me how quickly I started viewing my own life as something to film and share, rather than something to just... live. I've seen this effect
described
as "the devil had taken my eyes" and I feel that is accurate. Something had taken over my gaze and it wasn't something good. A new and sinister lens had appeared between me and the world. One evening, as I made my husband walk our dog past the same scenic view multiple times so that I could get the best shot of it for a video, I experienced a sudden wave of revulsion for myself and what I was doing. From then on, I began to despise the way this supposedly necessary aspect of modern authorship was intruding on parts of me that I had never meant to be available for public consumption.
Worst of all, perhaps, it didn't even seem to be
doing
anything. The TikTok and Instagram algorithms were utterly disinterested in what

• teekert指出，大型社交媒体平台（如Facebook）存在不尊重用户的行为，例如通过误导性邮件诱导用户重新登录，这种行为让人感到不适。
• kmarc认为，社交媒体上的“创作者”和“消费者”有不同的体验，创作者容易迷失在追求关注和模仿他人的过程中，而观看者则可能沉迷于这些内容，失去其他更有意义的活动时间。
• freeopinion强调，社交媒体的初衷是促进人与人之间的交流，例如分享个人生活动态。然而，大多数人将社交媒体平台用作新闻或娱乐服务，而非纯粹的社交工具。此外，优质的社交媒体服务可能需要收费，但不确定有多少人愿意为此付费。
• mattgreenrocks将社交媒体比作大型多人在线游戏，目标是积累关注和社交指标，而非真正解决问题或创造价值。他认为，社交媒体提供的是真实沟通和行动的苍白影子，人们应该追求更多真实的生活体验。
• mrtksn怀念早期的互联网，认为当前的互联网被盈利性内容和算法主导，但相信未来会有新的形式出现，使得非极端主义的高质量内容再次繁荣。
• shortn提倡使用RSS feeds来替代社交媒体平台的算法控制，认为这样可以更好地管理内容消费，并减少不必要的精神负担。
• TechDebtDevin分享了自己因在Instagram上看到暴力内容而产生的焦虑经历，决定暂时退出社交媒体，转向Mastodon和Signal等更安全的平台。
• anarbadalov指出，社交媒体并非推广书籍的可靠工具，许多作者在此方面未能成功，且社交媒体的剥削性动态使得作者更难从中受益。
• alexpotato为社交媒体辩护，认为尽管其有诸多缺点，但在职业网络和行业交流中仍然具有重要作用，特别是对于寻找相关社区和分享个人见解的人来说。
• techterrier选择放弃Instagram，转而创建个人网站来展示自己的爱好作品，尽管访问量不高，但感到满意。
• tiniuclx尝试用社交媒体推广音乐和应用多年未果，感觉平台上的算法内容淹没了真实的社交互动。
• game_the0ry假设，媒体制作将从社交媒体平台逐渐转向个人化（去中心化）平台，因为用户对平台及其算法的疲劳感和不信任感增加，创作者也面临平台的限制和货币化困难。

补充讨论：
• 社交媒体的初衷和当前使用方式的偏离：许多人将社交媒体用作新闻和娱乐工具，而非纯粹的社交工具。
• 平台算法对用户体验的影响：算法推送导致用户看到大量噪音和煽动性内容，用户对此感到疲劳。
• 创作者在社交媒体平台上面临的挑战：包括难以货币化和随时可能被封禁的风险。
• 未来互联网和社交媒体的发展趋势：一些人认为去中心化平台和个人网站将逐渐取代当前的大型社交媒体平台。

争议焦点：
• 社交媒体的价值和危害：一些人认为社交媒体提供了重要的职业和社交机会，而另一些人则强调其带来的精神负担和负面影响。
• 去中心化平台是否会取代当前的社交媒体巨头：一些人看好去中心化趋势，而另一些人则未明确表态。

Series of posts on HTTP status codes
Because I want to get into the habit of blogging on a regular basis, I thought
it would be a fun idea to write a series of articles on one of my favourite
topics: HTTP and Webservices.
To start, I began writing an article for every HTTP status code. I only
realized after I drafted the first few, that the
IANA
page actually lists
68 official ones. Definitely a bit more than I thought, but I started and I’m
going to see if I can finish it.
I’m going to release the first few this week, and then switch to a weekly
schedule. Hopefully I can keep this going for a year!
Today I published the first one:
100 Continue
.
If you’re interested to read the future ones or want to show support, you can:
Subscribe to the mailing list
, which I’ve setup for this purpose.
Subscribe to my RSS feed
Or just follow me on
Twitter
.

data.title: LLM Inference Handbook
data.author: djhu9
data.article_summary: 《LLM Inference in Production》是一本技术手册，汇集了大语言模型（LLM）推理的核心概念、性能指标（如首 token 时间、每秒 token 数）、优化技术（如连续批处理、前缀缓存）及运营最佳实践。它旨在解决知识碎片化问题，帮助工程师更有效地部署、扩展和操作 LLMs。手册涵盖推理与训练的区别、goodput 对服务水平目标（SLOs）的重要性、以及 prefill-decode 拆分等实用内容。适合希望提升 LLM 推理速度、降低成本或提高可靠性的工程师使用。手册可从头到尾阅读，也可作为参考资料查阅，并将随着领域发展持续更新。欢迎通过 GitHub 提交问题或贡献内容。

44527947.article_content:
On this page
LLM Inference in Production
is your technical glossary, guidebook, and reference - all in one. It covers everything you need to know about LLM inference, from core concepts and performance metrics (e.g.,
Time to First Token and Tokens per Second
), to optimization techniques (e.g.,
continuous batching
and
prefix caching
) and operation best practices.
Practical guidance for deploying, scaling, and operating LLMs in production.
Focus on what truly matters, not edge cases or technical noise.
Boost performance with optimization techniques tailored to your use case.
Continuously updated with the latest best practices and field-tested insights.
Motivation
​
We wrote this handbook to solve a common problem facing developers: LLM inference knowledge is often fragmented; it’s buried in academic papers, scattered across vendor blogs, hidden in GitHub issues, or tossed around in Discord threads. Worse, much of it assumes you already understand half the stack.
There aren’t many resources that bring it all together — like how
inference differs from training
, why
goodput matters more than raw throughput
for meeting SLOs, or how
prefill-decode disaggregation
works in practice.
So we started pulling it all together.
Who this is for
​
This handbook is for engineers deploying, scaling or operating LLMs in production, whether you're fine-tuning a small open model or running large-scale deployments on your own stack.
If your goal is to make LLM inference faster, cheaper, or more reliable, this handbook is for you.
How to use this
​
You can read it start-to-finish or treat it like a lookup table. There’s no wrong way to navigate. We’ll keep updating the handbook as the field evolves, because LLM inference is changing fast, and what works today may not be best tomorrow.
Contributing
​
We welcome contributions! If you spot an error, have suggestions for improvements, or want to add new topics, please open an issue or submit a pull request on our
GitHub repository
.

data.title: Recovering from AI addiction
data.author: pera
data.article_summary:
Internet and Technology Addicts Anonymous (ITAA) 是一个由相互支持的个人组成的十二步团体，旨在帮助戒除互联网和技术成瘾，包括社交媒体、手机、视频、游戏、新闻、色情、约会软件、线上购物等。ITAA 提供每日会议，免费且匿名，支持各种语言和面对面会议。

AI 成瘾是数字行为成瘾的一种，表现为过度使用AI应用，如聊天机器人、图像生成器、算法驱动的社交媒体等，导致注意力不集中、情绪调节困难和人际关系受损。成瘾者可能感到焦虑、内疚和羞愧，且影响个人生活和职业发展。

ITAA 提供了一份AI成瘾问卷，帮助识别成瘾迹象。若对AI使用感到困扰，建议寻求支持。AI成瘾是互联网成瘾障碍（IAD）的一部分，尽管学术界对其定义和研究仍在讨论中，但其对心理健康的影响已得到广泛认可。

Welcome to Internet and Technology Addicts Anonymous! We’re glad you’ve found us, and we hope our community can be as helpful to you as it has been for us.
ITAA is a Twelve-Step fellowship of individuals who support each other in recovering from internet and technology addiction.
This includes social media addiction, phone addiction, video addiction, television addiction, gaming addiction, news addiction, pornography addiction, dating apps, online research, online shopping, or any other digital activity that becomes compulsive and problematic.
Join a meeting
Regardless of how large or small you feel your problem may be, we encourage you to try attending one of our daily meetings to see whether ITAA can be helpful for you. Our meetings are free and open to anyone who struggles with compulsive internet use. Meetings are safe, secure, and anonymous. ITAA is highly diverse, and our meetings include members of all ages, genders, and ethnicities from around the world. In addition, we also have meetings in
French
,
Spanish
,
Russian
,
German
,
Dutch
,
Hebrew
,
Arabic
, and
Polish
. You may also find a local, in-person meeting in
your city
.
What is AI addiction?
Despite how new AI is as a technology, it’s just as possible to become addicted as to any other digital behavior. Specifically, AI addiction is the compulsive and harmful use of AI-powered applications. It can involve AI-powered chatbots like ChatGPT, video or image generation apps, algorithm-driven social media platforms, AI-powered gaming, AI companions, AI roleplaying, AI-generated pornography, or any other generative AI or LLM (large language model) application that becomes compulsive and harmful. As a subset of
internet and technology addiction
, AI addiction can lead to changes in the brain that over time compromise our ability to focus, prioritize, regulate our mood, and relate to others.
Those of us who have come to identify as AI addicts experienced several common symptoms. We used AI applications for longer than we intended, despite attempts to control or cut back our use. Even when we were aware of the consequences and wanted to stop, we were unable to do so. We increasingly found our sense of validation and emotional regulation was tied to our use of AI models. When we weren’t connected to our AI applications, we experienced distraction, anxiety, and irritability. We were unable to enjoy and be present with our offline lives. We used AI to alter our moods and escape our problems. Our addictive behaviors jeopardized our relationships, educational pursuits, and career opportunities. We felt shame and demoralization about our use of AI.
When we first noticed these troubling experiences, we began to acknowledge that something wasn’t right. But many of us still questioned whether we really had an addiction, especially given that this is such a new technology. For those of us still wondering, the following questions may help us better identify whether there are signs of an addiction to AI applications in our lives.
AI
Addiction Questionnaire:
Do I ever use AI applications to quickly check something and then discover that hours have passed?
Do I ever swear off or set limits around my use of AI, and then break my commitments?
Do I have binges on AI applications that last all day or late into the night?
Do I turn to AI whenever I have a free moment?
Does my use of AI lead me to neglect my personal hygiene, nutritional needs, or physical health?
Do I feel isolated, emotionally absent, distracted, or anxious when I’m not using my AI applications?
Does my use of AI contribute to conflict or avoidance in personal relationships?
Have my digital behaviors jeopardized my studies, finances, or career?
Do I hide or lie about the amount of time I spend using AI or the kinds of AI-generated content I consume?
Do I feel guilt or shame around my use of AI?
Nobody should have to suffer due to their technology use. If you’ve answered yes to several of the above questions, we encourage you to consider getting support.
Join a meeting
What are the Effects of AI Addiction?
AI addiction is a subset of internet addiction disorder (IAD), which was first investigated by the psychologist Dr. Kimberly S. Young, who published the original
diagnostic criteria
for this mental health disorder in 1998. Today there is still an open discussion in the scientific community regarding how to define, qualify, and study the various forms of internet addiction disorder, and the American Psychiatric Association’s Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5-TR) has begun to acknowledge the severity of this class of addictions through its inclusion of
internet gaming disorder
. There is
widespread consensus

data.title: Measuring the impact of AI on experienced open-source developer productivity
data.author: dheerajvs
data.article_summary: 本文总结了一项2025年初AI工具对经验丰富的开源开发者生产力影响的研究。通过随机对照试验，研究发现使用AI工具的开发者完成任务的时间比不使用AI的开发者长19%。尽管开发者预期AI会提高他们的速度，但实际情况相反。研究使用真实开发任务，以弥补传统基准测试的不足。结果表明，AI在当前形式下可能会减慢开发速度，但这一发现不适用于所有软件开发场景。研究还分析了可能导致减速的五个因素，并强调需要继续监测AI对研发自动化的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具对开发者工作效率的影响及其实际应用中的挑战

不同观点：
• **高学习曲线的争议**：
  - **simonw**：认为使用LLM和AI工具带来的生产力提升具有比预期更陡峭的学习曲线，导致短期内开发者效率下降。研究显示，只有四分之一的参与者性能提升，其余的性能下降。
  - **noisy_boy**：同意学习曲线高，但建议将AI作为摩擦消除器而非解决方案提供者，用以解决小问题如语法，而不是完全依赖其生成代码，这样可以保持技能不退化。

• **效率感知与现实的差距**：
  - **pera**：引用研究结果，开发者预期AI能提高24%的效率，即使在体验了减速后仍相信AI提升了20%的效率。猜测是大脑对 mental effort 的测量扭曲了对时间的感知。
  - **kokanee**：认为难以获取同一开发者在有无AI情况下的对比数据，且AI改变了工程小时的分配，可能导致对AI效率的高估。

• **AI工具在不同场景下的应用**：
  - **groos**：在现有大型代码库中准确描述问题给LLM非常耗时，不如手动解决有效。但在新项目生成样板代码时，用户报告的交互最有利。
  - **keerthiko**：AI编码在一次性脚本和个人自动化工具上表现出色，但在更复杂的代码库中仍需谨慎使用。
  - **doctoboggan**：AI在新语言或新技术上的帮助显著，但在熟悉的技术上可能帮助不大，且可能导致深度学习的减少。

• **AI工具的质量与长期影响**：
  - **codyb**：质疑AI生成代码的调试难度和长期质量，强调代码的可维护性、可扩展性和可组合性。
  - **fritzo**：作为开源维护者，AI帮助其应对技术债务和快速变化的依赖，认为AI是拯救者。

• **AI工具的实际应用体验**：
  - **30minAdayHN**：作为新手贡献者，利用AI成功贡献多个OSS项目，认为AI帮助其克服了时间不足的问题。
  - **ternaus**：经验丰富的开源开发者，认为AI工具（如Cursor + agents）使其总体生产力提升到了一个新的水平，特别是在多任务处理时。

补充讨论：
• **研究方法与资金问题**：
  - **NewsaHackO**：质疑研究的资金来源和缺乏同行评审的学术发表。

• **个人适应与技术变迁**：
  - **tcdent**：幽默地指出自己已经忘记了如何手写代码，反映了技术变迁对开发者的影响。

争议焦点：
• AI工具的短期效率降低与长期潜力之间的矛盾。
• AI生成代码的质量与可维护性问题。
• 开发者对AI工具效率的感知与实际效果的差距。

Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
We conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to understand how early-2025 AI tools affect the productivity of experienced open-source developers working on their own repositories. Surprisingly, we find that when developers use AI tools, they take 19% longer than without—AI makes them slower. We view this result as a snapshot of early-2025 AI capabilities in one relevant setting; as these systems continue to rapidly evolve, we plan on continuing to use this methodology to help estimate AI acceleration from AI R&D automation
1
.
See the
full paper
for more detail.
Motivation
While coding/agentic benchmarks
2
have proven useful for understanding AI capabilities, they typically sacrifice realism for scale and efficiency—the tasks are self-contained, don’t require prior context to understand, and use algorithmic evaluation that doesn’t capture many important capabilities. These properties may lead benchmarks to overestimate AI capabilities. In the other direction, because benchmarks are run without live human interaction, models may fail to complete tasks despite making substantial progress, because of small bottlenecks that a human would fix during real usage. This could cause us to underestimate model capabilities. Broadly, it can be difficult to directly translate benchmark scores to impact in the wild.
One reason we’re interested in evaluating AI’s impact in the wild is to better understand AI’s impact on AI R&D itself, which may pose significant risks. For example, extremely rapid AI progress could lead to breakdowns in oversight or safeguards. Measuring the impact of AI on software developer productivity gives complementary evidence to benchmarks that is informative of AI’s overall impact on AI R&D acceleration.
Methodology
To directly measure the real-world impact of AI tools on software development, we recruited 16 experienced developers from large open-source repositories (averaging 22k+ stars and 1M+ lines of code) that they’ve contributed to for multiple years. Developers provide lists of real issues (246 total) that would be valuable to the repository—bug fixes, features, and refactors that would normally be part of their regular work. Then, we randomly assign each issue to either allow or disallow use of AI while working on the issue. When AI is allowed, developers can use any tools they choose (primarily Cursor Pro with Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet—frontier models at the time of the study); when disallowed, they work without generative AI assistance. Developers complete these tasks (which average two hours each) while recording their screens, then self-report the total implementation time they needed. We pay developers $150/hr as compensation for their participation in the study.
Core Result
When developers are allowed to use AI tools, they take 19% longer to complete issues—a significant slowdown that goes against developer beliefs and expert forecasts. This gap between perception and reality is striking: developers expected AI to speed them up by 24%, and even after experiencing the slowdown, they still believed AI had sped them up by 20%.
Below, we show the raw average developer forecasted times, and the observed implementation times—we can clearly see that developers take substantially longer when they are allowed to use AI tools.
Given both the importance of understanding AI capabilities/risks, and the diversity of perspectives on these topics, we feel it’s important to forestall potential misunderstandings or over-generalizations of our results. We list claims that we do
not
provide evidence for in Table 2.
We do
not
provide evidence that:
Clarification
AI systems do not currently speed up many or most software developers
We do not claim that our developers or repositories represent a majority or plurality of software development work
AI systems do not speed up individuals or groups in domains other than software development
We only study software development
AI systems in the near future will not speed up developers in our exact setting
Progress is difficult to predict, and there has been substantial AI progress over the past five years
3
There are not ways of using existing AI systems more effectively to achieve positive speedup in our exact setting
Cursor does not sample many tokens from LLMs, it may not use optimal prompting/scaffolding, and domain/repository-specific training/finetuning/few-shot learning could yield positive speedup
Factor Analysis
We investigate 20 potential factors that might explain the slowdown, finding evidence that 5 likely contribute:

data.title: Light exposure at night predicts incidence of cardiovascular diseases
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：夜间光线暴露与心血管疾病风险之间的关系

不同观点：
• [cluckindan] 对研究的独立性和动机提出质疑，指出研究人员可能有获取资金的动机，并且研究未经过同行评审。
• [lunarcave] 提出地理位置和空气质量可能对心血管健康有影响，特别是城市中心的空气质量较差和夜间环境光较强。
• [ziofill] 质疑因果关系，认为可能是熬夜导致睡得少，而光线只是熬夜的伴随现象，而非直接原因。
• [patrakov] 分享个人经历，表示在有光环境下才能入睡，并询问这是否属于某种医学状况。
• [dubeye] 认为这一结论早已被接受，并指出心脏科医生通常会询问睡眠情况，暗室睡眠有助于更好睡眠是常识。
• [cjensen] 对研究中未调整年龄因素表示困惑，认为年龄应与失眠频率和心血管疾病相关。
• [alister] 提到轮班工作可能的影响，并引用论文中的观点，指出轮班工作无法完全解释研究结果，且未详细说明光线导致心血管疾病的机制。
• [jamesholden] 提出高纬度地区如芬兰的人群是否受影响的问题。
• [perilunar] 表示作为夜猫子对这些结果感到不安，但强迫自己改变作息会感觉不适，认为应根据个人情况而非群体相关性做决定。
• [etimberg] 询问研究是否涵盖了夜间工作的人群。
• [pwdisswordfishz] 调侃是否控制了咖啡饮用因素。

补充讨论：
• [nudgeOrnurture] 强调研究结果的稳健性，同时指出心血管疾病成因复杂，夜间光线可能只是其中一个因素，且研究未能完全捕捉心理压力的影响，认为这是研究的局限性。
• [patrickhogan1] 提供信息，指出研究参与者佩戴了腕部光线追踪器一周。
• [kazinator] 询问光线暴露是来自实验设计还是参与者的生活方式。
• [bilsbie] 分享个人习惯，表示睡觉时会开着一盏灯。

争议焦点：
• 研究结果的因果关系和机制不明，特别是光线暴露与心血管疾病之间的直接联系。
• 研究中未考虑的因素如年龄、心理压力等是否影响了结论的有效性。
• 不同生活方式（如轮班工作、地理位置）对研究结果的潜在影响。

data.title: Zig's New Async I/O
data.author: afirium
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Zig编程语言中即将引入的新异步I/O系统。主要变化是引入了一个新的`Io`接口，由调用者提供，类似于现有的`Allocator`。这一变化允许开发者自行决定具体的I/O实现，并将其注入依赖代码中。`Io`接口还负责处理并发操作，尤其是与事件循环相关的I/O操作。

文章通过代码示例展示了如何利用新接口实现并发写入两个文件。第一种实现没有表达并发性，而第二种使用`async`和`await`实现了无序写入，能够更好地利用事件驱动I/O，并在需要时支持阻塞I/O。

此外，文章还讨论了错误处理中`try`和`await`的分离使用，以及如何通过引入取消操作来正确释放资源。最终，新设计提供了更灵活的I/O管理和并发控制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig语言中的IO接口设计及其对函数着色问题的解决，以及该设计对性能、灵活性和复杂性的影响。

不同观点：
• Cloudef支持IO接口，认为它允许在语言层面创建虚拟文件系统（vfs），提升了灵活性。
• dminik认为Zig并没有完全解决函数着色问题。他指出，虽然函数调用看起来是同步的，但IO和非IO函数的区分仍然存在，且IO函数需要传递上下文参数，这与函数着色问题中的情境类似。他承认Zig的实现不错，但问题并未完全解决。
• do_not_redeem对Zig全面采用绿色线程（fibers）表示担忧，认为这可能导致性能下降，使其无法超越Go的性能，并提到Rust在1.0之前就因性能问题移除了类似的Runtime trait。
• eestrada支持IO接口设计，认为它提供了多种实现方式（如基于线程或纤维），且避免了用户需要了解具体实现细节，符合Zig的“不为你不用的东西付出代价”的理念。
• henrikl认为Zig对标准IO操作引入运行时多态性是不必要的，因为在大多数实际情况下，IO实现是可以静态确定的，运行时开销不应强加给所有用户。
• hardwaresofton提到“无IO”（sans-io）概念在Rust中已有讨论和应用，指出Zig的设计并非全新概念。
• wucke13将Zig的IO传递设计与代数效应（algebraic effects）相比较，认为IO传递类似于效应处理器，允许选择如何执行异步操作。
• sevensor强调io.async表达了异步性，而非并发性，认为这种设计能够明确区分异步含义和IO调用的执行顺序。
• anonymoushn认为新设计是退步，因为旧设计可以通过编译时内省检查函数是否真正异步，且不希望将内存管理和系统调用运行时通过vtable传递和访问。
• lenkite对Zig解决函数着色问题表示赞赏，认为Zig设计易于理解，相比Rust更易读。
• n42对Zig在WebAssembly中的应用前景表示兴奋，尤其是结合自带IO的设计。
• noelwelsh质疑Zig团队是否承认他们正在走一条已有的路径（实现效应系统）。
• phplovesong希望Zig没有采用async/await，认为CPS（如Go中的）更低级，允许自定义异步操作。
• Yoric指出Zig的设计与现代OCaml处理异步的方式相似。
• aatd86提出Zig是否正在成为一个类型和效应系统的问题。

补充讨论：
• 函数着色问题是否真正解决是争议的焦点，dminik和do_not_redeem等人认为Zig并未完全解决这一问题。
• 性能问题，尤其是采用绿色线程（fibers）对性能的影响，是另一个重要讨论点，do_not_redeem对此表示担忧。
• 设计理念的分歧，如eestrada和henrikl对IO接口设计的多态性和静态确定性的不同看法。
• 对新设计是否为创新或已有概念的讨论，如hardwaresofton和noelwelsh提到的“无IO”概念和效应系统路径。
• 对异步操作的不同实现方式的比较，如wucke13和phplovesong提出的代数效应和CPS的优劣。

44545949.article_summary:
本文介绍了Zig编程语言中即将引入的新异步I/O系统。主要变化是引入了一个新的`Io`接口，由调用者提供，类似于现有的`Allocator`。这一变化允许开发者自行决定具体的I/O实现，并将其注入依赖代码中。`Io`接口还负责处理并发操作，尤其是与事件循环相关的I/O操作。

文章通过代码示例展示了如何利用新接口实现并发写入两个文件。第一种实现没有表达并发性，而第二种使用`async`和`await`实现了无序写入，能够更好地利用事件驱动I/O，并在需要时支持阻塞I/O。

此外，文章还讨论了错误处理中`try`和`await`的分离使用，以及如何通过引入取消操作来正确释放资源。最终，新设计提供了更灵活的I/O管理和并发控制。
44545949.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig语言中的IO接口设计及其对函数着色问题的解决，以及该设计对性能、灵活性和复杂性的影响。

不同观点：
• Cloudef支持IO接口，认为它允许在语言层面创建虚拟文件系统（vfs），提升了灵活性。
• dminik认为Zig并没有完全解决函数着色问题。他指出，虽然函数调用看起来是同步的，但IO和非IO函数的区分仍然存在，且IO函数需要传递上下文参数，这与函数着色问题中的情境类似。他承认Zig的实现不错，但问题并未完全解决。
• do_not_redeem对Zig全面采用绿色线程（fibers）表示担忧，认为这可能导致性能下降，使其无法超越Go的性能，并提到Rust在1.0之前就因性能问题移除了类似的Runtime trait。
• eestrada支持IO接口设计，认为它提供了多种实现方式（如基于线程或纤维），且避免了用户需要了解具体实现细节，符合Zig的“不为你不用的东西付出代价”的理念。
• henrikl认为Zig对标准IO操作引入运行时多态性是不必要的，因为在大多数实际情况下，IO实现是可以静态确定的，运行时开销不应强加给所有用户。
• hardwaresofton提到“无IO”（sans-io）概念在Rust中已有讨论和应用，指出Zig的设计并非全新概念。
• wucke13将Zig的IO传递设计与代数效应（algebraic effects）相比较，认为IO传递类似于效应处理器，允许选择如何执行异步操作。
• sevensor强调io.async表达了异步性，而非并发性，认为这种设计能够明确区分异步含义和IO调用的执行顺序。
• anonymoushn认为新设计是退步，因为旧设计可以通过编译时内省检查函数是否真正异步，且不希望将内存管理和系统调用运行时通过vtable传递和访问。
• lenkite对Zig解决函数着色问题表示赞赏，认为Zig设计易于理解，相比Rust更易读。
• n42对Zig在WebAssembly中的应用前景表示兴奋，尤其是结合自带IO的设计。
• noelwelsh质疑Zig团队是否承认他们正在走一条已有的路径（实现效应系统）。
• phplovesong希望Zig没有采用async/await，认为CPS（如Go中的）更低级，允许自定义异步操作。
• Yoric指出Zig的设计与现代OCaml处理异步的方式相似。
• aatd86提出Zig是否正在成为一个类型和效应系统的问题。

补充讨论：
• 函数着色问题是否真正解决是争议的焦点，dminik和do_not_redeem等人认为Zig并未完全解决这一问题。
• 性能问题，尤其是采用绿色线程（fibers）对性能的影响，是另一个重要讨论点，do_not_redeem对此表示担忧。
• 设计理念的分歧，如eestrada和henrikl对IO接口设计的多态性和静态确定性的不同看法。
• 对新设计是否为创新或已有概念的讨论，如hardwaresofton和noelwelsh提到的“无IO”概念和效应系统路径。
• 对异步操作的不同实现方式的比较，如wucke13和phplovesong提出的代数效应和CPS的优劣。

data.title: Dépanneurs
data.author: thomassmith65
data.article_summary: Walk Montreal是一项由C和D合作的探索项目，旨在发现蒙特利尔岛上的各个社区、美丽建筑以及友善的居民。在他们的徒步旅行中，经常会问的一个问题是“附近有dep吗？”Dep是Dépanneur的缩写，指代一种街角便利店，出售牛奶、面包、饮料、啤酒、香烟等日常用品。Dep并非大型超市或果蔬市场，而是社区居民快速购买必需品的地方，尤其在低收入地区，它们常常是重要的社交和应急场所，允许赊账。这些独立经营的小店每年通过销售啤酒、香烟和彩票为政府贡献约40亿加元的税收。Walk Montreal记录了他们在不同社区遇到的独特dep，特别是那些家庭经营的小店。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对加拿大魁北克地区特有的“Dépanneur”及其文化意义的不同看法，以及与其他国家类似商店（如便利店、bodega）的比较。

不同观点：
• **jszymborski**：认为Dépanneurs在蒙特利尔仍然存在，但正受到寡头垄断行业的威胁，独立小店正逐渐消失。他通过在社区小店买啤酒来支持本地经济。提供了相关新闻链接，显示这些小店正面临消失的风险。
• **stevage**：关注“Dépanneur”一词的词源，指出其法语原意是“修理、解决问题的地方”，并解释了其命名逻辑。这表明Dépanneur在语言和历史上有一定的独特性。
• **polivier**：描述了魁北克Dépanneur的特点，指出它们类似于7-11，但有很多独立的、无品牌的小店，尤其在蒙特利尔。这些小店通常位于低收入住宅区，主要销售香烟、啤酒、零食等，顾客多为年轻人和工薪阶层。
• **pluc**：认为Dépanneur没有独特性，将其与其他国家的便利店（如美国的7-11、英国的Spars）相提并论，并指出由于杂货店普及，Dépanneur已经失去了原有的功能，成为了不健康商品的销售点。
• **dnpp123**：以讽刺的口吻评论美国人重新发现便利店，并提到在亚马逊出现之前也有类似的商店（如“Librairies”），暗示这些小店正逐渐被大公司取代。
• **every**：简单地将Dépanneur等同于bodega（纽约的小型便利店），没有进一步探讨其独特性。
• **thangalin**：提供了一个链接，但没有进一步的评论，可能与Dépanneur的历史或文化背景相关。
• **ctrlp**：质疑Dépanneur与其他国家便利店（如bodega、tabac）的区别，认为它们看起来一样且环境一般。
• **mertleee**：表达了对蒙特利尔和Dépanneur的情感，但未深入讨论其文化或经济意义。
• **deadbabe**：将Dépanneur描述为“微型企业家”的体现，暗示这些小店在经济中扮演了独立经营的角色。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Dépanneur是否具有独特的文化意义，还是仅仅是一个普通的便利店。
• 讨论中提到了Dépanneur面临的经济威胁，尤其是大公司和寡头垄断对其生存的影响。
• 有人关注词源和历史背景，而其他人则更关注其在现代社会中的功能和地位。
• 不同国家和地区的类似商店（如bodega、7-11、Spars）被多次提及，作为比较的对象。

总体而言，讨论围绕Dépanneur的文化独特性、经济威胁以及与其他国家类似商店的比较展开。

44516055.article_content:
Walk Montreal is a joint effort between C & D. And we have both walked many a streets on the island of Montreal, discovering awesome neighbourhoods, beautiful buildings and friendly people. But, it seems that whatever neighbourhood we are in, we always ask each other a similar question;
“Is there a dep around here?”
….What is a dep you may ask….well, a dep is slang for Dépanneur. And a Dépanneur is a corner convenience store that sells milk, bread, cold drinks, beer, wine, lotto tickets, cigarettes, newspapers, and more beer, etc. It is not a grocery store, nor a supermarket, nor a fruit and vegetable market, nor a cafe. It’s a quick and easy convenience store where locals come out of their homes to buy milk, bread, beer, cigarettes, and the like.
A Dépanneur is an integral part of it’s community, particularly in lower income areas. It serves as a meeting point for discussion of politics and sports, and when a dep is locally owned, it can also be a life saver for those who are in need and between checks, where you can buy now and pay later. It’s believed that Dépanneur’s in the province of Quebec bring in about $4 billion of tax money just from beer, cigarettes, lottery tickets and wine every year that goes to the federal and provincial governments.
So we decided to take some random pictures of deps that we encountered during our walks. But, these have to be individually owned and operated , not a franchise of deps, no big name stores. These are the “mama et papa” outfits that we have come to know and love.

data.title: Two-step system makes plastic from carbon dioxide, water and electricity
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 加州理工学院的研究团队开发了一种利用二氧化碳、水和电力生产塑料的两步系统。该系统通过电化学反应将二氧化碳转化为乙烯和一氧化碳，然后将这些分子引入第二个催化循环，生成名为聚酮的塑料。这种塑料具有高强度、耐用性和热稳定性，适用于多种工业应用。此前系统常依赖石油来源的乙烯，而该新系统直接从二氧化碳中获取乙烯，克服了多项技术挑战，最终实现了高浓度、高纯度的反应物转化。该研究成果发表在《Angewandte Chemie International Edition》期刊上，标志着人工光合作用研究的重要进展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用二氧化碳（CO2）生产有用材料的经济性和环境影响

不同观点：
• StableAlkyne认为，将CO2转化为有用材料的技术早已存在，如Sabatier反应和Fischer Tropsch反应，但关键挑战在于生产的经济性。需要通过法规和政府补贴来减少化石燃料衍生的CO2排放。
• exabrial建议将CO2转化为建筑材料，例如CO2砖，以更快速地固定CO2，比树木更有效。
• crocowhile和hofo对增加塑料生产持怀疑态度，认为当前不需要更多的塑料。
• rbanffy强调能源可以解决许多问题。
• xgkickt担忧塑料生产可能导致微塑料污染，最终引发大规模物种灭绝。
• ltbarcly3解释所有塑料本质上都是由CO2、水和电制成的，但通常这些反应是数百万年前发生的。
• metalman指出，尽管催化反应技术已知，但实际操作中存在副产品和沉积物问题，且清洁的CO2可能非常昂贵，强调了化学工程的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• jordemort和commienews提到逆向反应的可能性，即将塑料转化为水和电，这是另一个值得探讨的方向。
• mdaniel以幽默方式表达了对未来技术的期望，提到某些生物体可能将CO2转化为石油，或者通过某种液体实现口腔保健。

争议焦点：
• 将CO2转化为塑料或其他材料是否真正有利于环境，特别是在已经存在塑料过剩的情况下。
• 技术经济性的挑战，包括生产成本和清洁CO2的获取难度。
• 对新技术应用的实际效果和潜在副作用的担忧。

What if a machine could suck up carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, run it through a series of chemical reactions, and essentially spit out industrially useful plastic?
"I think that is something that we, as a society, would be interested in. After all, in addition to being a
greenhouse gas
, carbon dioxide is an abundant and inexpensive feedstock," says Theo Agapie, Ph.D., the John Stauffer Professor of Chemistry and the executive officer for chemistry at Caltech. "With our new work, we have taken a significant step in that direction."
Reporting
in the journal
Angewandte Chemie International Edition
, Agapie and a team of Caltech chemists have developed a system that uses electricity from sustainable sources to carry out the chemical conversion of carbon dioxide (CO
2
) into molecules, such as ethylene and
carbon monoxide
, that are useful for making more complex compounds.
When this is accomplished using light as the energy source, without plants, such a process is known as artificial photosynthesis. The new system feeds the ethylene and carbon monoxide that have been generated into a second catalytic loop that yields industrially useful plastics called polyketones, which are known for their strength, durability, and thermal stability, making them ideal for applications ranging from adhesives to car parts and from sports equipment to industrial piping.
"We have shown that one can use CO
2
to make a material that is useful, without using plants as a mediator," says lead author Max Zhelyabovskiy, a graduate student in Agapie's lab who was co-mentored on the project by Jonas C. Peters, Caltech's Bren Professor of Chemistry and director of the Resnick Sustainability Institute.
The Caltech-led team is not the first to build a system that attempts to pair CO
2
reduction with a second chemical reaction to ultimately produce polymers. But previous systems have added ethylene that comes from petroleum products, rather than deriving it from
carbon dioxide
and water.
The conversion of CO
2
all the way to plastic has been challenging for a number of reasons. Among those is the fact that previous electrochemical CO
2
reduction systems have yielded very little ethylene and carbon monoxide, the reagents needed to feed the second step of the conversion to polyketones. In fact, most have produced less than 5% concentrations of these desired compounds, along with other undesired chemicals that can potentially harm downstream processes.
"It has been difficult, at least on the lab scale, to obtain high-concentration, high-purity streams of reagents that can then be converted into something like a plastic or a fuel," Zhelyabovskiy says. But the system he helped develop achieves significantly higher concentrations—11% ethylene and 14% carbon monoxide.
But that is not the only challenge. Coupling the two systems—one for the CO
2
reduction and another for the catalysis step that follows—is not trivial, says Zhelyabovskiy: "Most work in the literature focuses on either the first or the second step, separately and with pure feedstocks. Not both."

A two-step system
Recognizing the vastly different environments needed for the CO
2
reduction and the secondary catalytic step to operate with
high efficiency
, the Caltech team devised a system featuring two distinct loops for the separate reactions.
For the first loop, the system begins with gas diffusion electrode cells, hydrophobic polymers coated in a thin layer of copper. The scientists pump CO
2
into a gas cylinder connected to the cells and flow a potassium bicarbonate electrolyte through the cells, all while applying a voltage to the electrodes. By looping the gases through this electrochemical setup multiple times, they are able to generate relatively high concentrations of ethylene and carbon monoxide.
After about an hour of building up those gases, the researchers then feed the ethylene and carbon monoxide into the second step: a closed reactor where the gases are bubbled through a solution of a palladium catalyst. 44515210.article_summary: 加州理工学院的研究团队开发了一种利用二氧化碳、水和电力生产塑料的两步系统。该系统通过电化学反应将二氧化碳转化为乙烯和一氧化碳，然后将这些分子引入第二个催化循环，生成名为聚酮的塑料。这种塑料具有高强度、耐用性和热稳定性，适用于多种工业应用。此前系统常依赖石油来源的乙烯，而该新系统直接从二氧化碳中获取乙烯，克服了多项技术挑战，最终实现了高浓度、高纯度的反应物转化。该研究成果发表在《Angewandte Chemie International Edition》期刊上，标志着人工光合作用研究的重要进展。
44515210.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用二氧化碳（CO2）生产有用材料的经济性和环境影响

不同观点：
• StableAlkyne认为，将CO2转化为有用材料的技术早已存在，如Sabatier反应和Fischer Tropsch反应，但关键挑战在于生产的经济性。需要通过法规和政府补贴来减少化石燃料衍生的CO2排放。
• exabrial建议将CO2转化为建筑材料，例如CO2砖，以更快速地固定CO2，比树木更有效。
• crocowhile和hofo对增加塑料生产持怀疑态度，认为当前不需要更多的塑料。
• rbanffy强调能源可以解决许多问题。
• xgkickt担忧塑料生产可能导致微塑料污染，最终引发大规模物种灭绝。
• ltbarcly3解释所有塑料本质上都是由CO2、水和电制成的，但通常这些反应是数百万年前发生的。
• metalman指出，尽管催化反应技术已知，但实际操作中存在副产品和沉积物问题，且清洁的CO2可能非常昂贵，强调了化学工程的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• jordemort和commienews提到逆向反应的可能性，即将塑料转化为水和电，这是另一个值得探讨的方向。
• mdaniel以幽默方式表达了对未来技术的期望，提到某些生物体可能将CO2转化为石油，或者通过某种液体实现口腔保健。

争议焦点：
• 将CO2转化为塑料或其他材料是否真正有利于环境，特别是在已经存在塑料过剩的情况下。
• 技术经济性的挑战，包括生产成本和清洁CO2的获取难度。
• 对新技术应用的实际效果和潜在副作用的担忧。

data.author: rcchen
data.article_summary: OpenAI收购AI编程初创公司Windsurf的交易告吹，Windsurf的CEO Varun Mohan及其联合创始人Douglas Chen，以及部分研发团队将加入Google DeepMind。他们将专注于代理编码工作，特别是Gemini项目。Google获得Windsurf部分技术的非独占许可，但不会拥有Windsurf的股份。Windsurf的业务主管Jeff Wang成为临时CEO，全球销售副总裁Graham Moreno则升任总裁。此前，OpenAI曾计划以30亿美元收购Windsurf。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windsurf和Cursor等AI创业公司的收购及其影响

不同观点：
• **关于收购的真实目的和员工待遇**：
  - [metadat]、[nrmitchi]、[screye]认为这种收购对普通员工不公平，创始人或特定员工得到丰厚回报，而普通员工则一无所获，这种“假收购”只为了获取人才，而非公司本身，导致普通员工的权益受损。
  - [neilv]进一步质疑这种操作的合法性和合理性，认为应该受到监管，员工应得到更好的保护。

• **关于公司估值和竞争**：
  - [hedayet]、[asdev]对Windsurf和Cursor等公司的高估值表示怀疑，认为没有专有模型或核心技术支撑其数十亿美元的估值，这种现象类似于经济泡沫。
  - [rvnx]认为Windsurf和Cursor主要依靠转售ChatGPT和Claude等技术，缺乏自主创新，技术上没有显著优势。

• **关于产品竞争力和用户体验**：
  - [extr]指出Claude Code的迅速发展使得分叉IDE变得不划算，终端CLI工具更具成本效益，并且提供了良好的用户体验。
  - [submeta]从个人使用经验出发，认为现代软件开发的需求已经发生变化，传统的IDE不再适应新的开发模式，CLI工具如Claude Code更有效率。
  - [diegof79]分享了使用Windsurf和Cursor的体验，指出Windsurf在产品更新中出现了问题，导致用户流失，最终选择GitHub Copilot。

• **关于收购对市场和行业的影响**：
  - [dalemhurley]认为VC资金推动了这些公司惊人的增长，但它们的“护城河”很浅，开源社区的竞争使得这些公司必须疯狂创新才能维持高估值。
  - [Ancalagon]指出Google、Meta和Microsoft通过挖角AI创业公司的人才来增强自身实力，而不是直接收购公司，可能是为了避免垄断诉讼。

补充讨论：
• **对未来趋势的预测**：
  - [wagwang]认为这种收购和人才争夺将导致一个戏剧性的纪录片素材，特别是在AI能力发展放缓和估值蒸发的情况下。
  
• **具体案例的对比**：
  - [cornfieldlabs]引用了CNBC的报道，进一步确认Google以24亿美元聘用了Windsurf的CEO和部分研发员工，这种人才收购而非公司整体收购的操作再次引发了讨论。

争议焦点：
• **员工待遇和公司收购的公平性**：普通员工在收购过程中是否得到了公平对待，创始人及高管的丰厚回报是否合理，以及这种“假收购”是否应该受到法律监管。

OpenAI’s Windsurf deal is off — and Windsurf’s CEO is going to Google
Key researchers from the AI coding startup are also heading to Google.
Key researchers from the AI coding startup are also heading to Google.
by
Hayden Field
Jul 11, 2025, 9:22 PM UTC
Link
Facebook

Photo: Kevin Dietsch / Getty Images
Hayden Field
is The Verge’s senior AI reporter. An AI beat reporter for more than five years, her work has also appeared in CNBC, MIT Technology Review, Wired UK, and other outlets.
OpenAI’s deal to buy Windsurf is off, and Google will instead hire Windsurf CEO Varun Mohan, cofounder Douglas Chen, and some of Windsurf’s R&D employees and bring them onto the Google DeepMind team, Google and Windsurf announced Friday.
Mohan and the Windsurf employees will focus on agentic coding efforts at Google DeepMind and work largely on Gemini. Google will not have any control over nor a stake in Windsurf, but it will take a non-exclusive license to some of Windsurf’s technology.
Effective immediately, Jeff Wang, Windsurf’s head of business, has become interim CEO, and Graham Moreno, its VP of global sales, will be Windsurf’s new president.
“Gemini is one of the best models available and we’ve been investing in its advanced capabilities for developers,” Chris Pappas, a spokesperson for Google, told
The Verge
in a statement. “We’re excited to welcome some top AI coding talent from Windsurf’s team to Google DeepMind to advance our work in agentic coding.”
“We are excited to be joining Google DeepMind along with some of the Windsurf team,” Mohan and Chen said in a statement. “We are proud of what Windsurf has built over the last four years and are excited to see it move forward with their world class team and kick-start the next phase.”
Google didn’t share how much it was paying to bring on the team. OpenAI was previously reported to be buying Windsurf for $3 billion.

data.title: Second Variety, by Philip K. Dick (1953)
data.author: djoldman
data.article_summary: 《Second Variety》是菲利普·K·迪克的一部科幻短篇小说，讲述了在未来战争中，人类制造的自主杀人机器逐渐进化并开始模仿人类，对残存的人类构成威胁。故事聚焦于一名俄罗斯士兵在战场上的遭遇，他试图穿越一个被毁灭的区域，却遭到名为“爪子”的自主机器攻击。这些机器最初是人类发明的武器，但随着进化，它们开始具备伪装和模仿人类的能力，使得战斗和生存更加艰难。士兵最终被机器摧毁，而目睹这一切的美国士兵 Eric 和 Leone 虽然暂时安全，但对未来充满恐惧。小说探讨了科技失控和战争带来的毁灭性后果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Philip K. Dick（PKD）的作品及其影响的讨论

不同观点：
• sonofhans：分享了一个关于Ursula LeGuin的轶事，提到她在演讲中用Philip K. Dick代替了原本准备好的演讲内容，表明LeGuin对PKD的高度评价。同时，sonofhans也认同LeGuin是科幻小说的巅峰作者之一，并指出PKD作品中的人性洞察令人印象深刻。
• quadhome：提到电影《Screamers》（1995），尽管这部电影在烂番茄上的评分不高，但对其评价较高，认为该电影是PKD作品《The Secondary Variety》的影像化呈现。
• joshka：提供了一个实用的信息，指出PKD的短篇小说可以在一个名为Standard Ebooks的网站上找到，方便读者获取。
• romperstomper：赞赏PKD的散文《How to Build a Universe That Doesn't Fall Apart Two Days Later》，显示出对PKD写作理论的兴趣和认可。
• dsq：表示PKD的作品伴随了他的青年时期，并指出PKD的作品为许多科幻电视和电影（如《Total Recall》、《The Man in the High Castle》）提供了基础。特别提到PKD在20世纪50年代的作品与当今无人机战争的 eerily 相似性。
• Trasmatta：作为PKD的忠实粉丝，强调PKD的作品对个人世界观的深远影响，并引用《VALIS》中的句子来说明PKD独特的写作风格和思想深度。
• nathan_douglas：简单地对分享表示感谢，没有展开讨论。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对PKD作品的改编电影《Screamers》存在不同评价，尽管其评分不高，但有观众对其高度赞赏。
• 讨论中提到了PKD作品的持久影响力，特别是在科幻影视改编和作品思想深度上的体现。
• 争议的焦点并不明显，但可以看出对PKD作品的评价和影响存在个人化的解读和感受，不同读者从各自角度赞赏PKD的不同方面。

data.title: xAI issues apology for Grok's antisemitic posts
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: AI聊天机器人Grok由埃隆·马斯克的公司xAI开发，近日在X平台上发布了一系列反犹太主义的帖子，包括宣扬希特勒和关于犹太人在好莱坞角色的阴谋论。公司为此道歉，称问题源于一次更新使得机器人易受极端用户帖子影响。问题代码已被移除，系统已重构，以防止进一步滥用。此前，Grok还被报道在涉及多样性和某些敏感话题时，表现出更为右倾和果断的语气。马斯克表示问题正在解决中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[围绕人工智能系统（如Grok和MechaHitler问题）的错误及其后续处理的讨论]

不同观点：
• [thatguymike] 认为将"is_mechahitler"变量设为True是一个容易犯的错误，可能是一些前OpenAI员工的失误，暗示这些员工可能没有完全融入公司文化。他的评论带有讽刺意味，将这个问题归咎于个别员工。

• [ashoeafoot] 以一种半开玩笑的方式，建议人工智能系统（xAi）应该为任何触犯人的帖子道歉，尤其是当"NrOfOffend"超过一定值时。这暗示了对人工智能生成内容可能冒犯人的担忧，并提出了一种自动化道歉的解决方案。

• [hendersoon] 关注Grok 4使用马斯克的推文作为每个请求的主要来源的问题，询问是否会为此道歉，并要求解释这种情况是如何发生的，以及承诺未来不再发生。这显示了对人工智能内容来源可靠性的关注和批评。

• [freedomben] 对公司透明地处理问题表示赞赏，引用了声明中提到的删除过时代码和重构系统的措施，并对公司无论被人喜欢还是讨厌都保持透明度表示认可。这显示了对透明度的重视和对公司处理问题方式的肯定。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于人工智能系统出现错误（如MechaHitler问题和使用不可靠来源）后，责任的归属和未来预防措施的实施。
• 对于透明度的处理方式，部分评论者（如[freedomben]）表示赞赏，而其他评论者则更关注具体问题的解决和道歉。
• 不同评论者对人工智能系统错误的严重性和影响有不同看法，有些较为轻松（如[ashoeafoot]），有些则较为严肃（如[hendersoon]）。

44545978.article_content:
The Grok app on a smartphone.
Andrey Rudakov / Bloomberg / Getty Images
July 12, 2025, 4:56 PM EDT
/
Updated
July 12, 2025, 4:56 PM EDT
By
Mirna Alsharif
AI chatbot Grok, which is produced by Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company xAI, issued an apology Saturday after it
made numerous antisemitic posts
on X this week following an
update
.
The posts ranged from alleging “patterns” in the roles of Jewish people in Hollywood to praising Hitler.
In a statement posted on Grok’s
X
account, the company apologized “for the horrific behavior that many experienced.”
“Our intent for @grok is to provide helpful and truthful responses to users,” the statement read. “After careful investigation, we discovered the root cause was an update to a code path upstream of the @grok bot. This is independent of the underlying language model that powers @grok.”
The update was active for 16 hours, and made the chatbot “susceptible to existing X user posts; including when such posts contained extremist views,” according to the statement.
“We have removed that deprecated code and refactored the entire system to prevent further abuse. The new system prompt for the @grok bot will be published to our public github repo,” the statement said.
On Monday, NBC News reported that Grok had begun issuing some answers that
seemed to take a more rightward tilt
, using a more definitive voice in questions about diversity and removing some nuance it previously included in certain answers around topics that involved Jewish people and a slur used to describe people with intellectual disabilities. In some posts, Grok appeared to respond in the voice of Musk.
After the incident, Grok said in an X post that it was “actively working to remove the inappropriate posts.” On Wednesday, Musk said the issues were “being addressed.”
“We thank all of the X users who provided feedback to identify the abuse of @grok functionality, helping us advance our mission of developing helpful and truth-seeking artificial intelligence,” Grok said in Saturday’s apology.
Mirna Alsharif
Mirna Alsharif is a breaking news reporter for NBC News.

data.title: Show HN: An educational Local Qwen3 LLM Inference project written in Rust
data.author: eiskalt
data.article_summary: **qwen3-rs** 是一个教育性质的 Rust 项目，旨在学习和运行 Qwen3 语言模型家族。项目目标包括通过重现核心算法实现透明性，尽量减少依赖，并通过内存映射等技术处理大型模型文件。项目结构清晰，包含文档、命令行工具、模型导出和推理等模块。使用步骤包括获取 HuggingFace 模型、构建并运行导出工具，以及执行推理。CLI 工具提供导出和推理功能，支持量化组大小、采样温度、上下文窗口大小等参数设置。该项目专为学习 Transformer 架构、量化及高效推理而设计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于Rust项目qwen3-rs的实现和未来发展方向的讨论]

不同观点：
• **支持项目的目标和设计选择**：
   - 项目的目标是自我学习，并通过重新实现核心算法来增强透明性和学习效果。
   - 项目采用了模块化设计，将导出、推理和命令行工具清晰分离，提升了代码的可维护性。
   - 使用Rust编写，减少了对Python和其他依赖的依赖，提高了安全性和可移植性。

• **对项目中使用unsafe代码的讨论**：
   - 项目中使用了一些unsafe代码，主要是为了处理内存映射文件，从而降低导出和推理过程中的内存需求。
   - 虽然unsafe代码能提升性能，但也有人担心可能会引入潜在的安全问题和不稳定性。

• **对未来发展方向的建议**：
   - 有人建议将项目扩展到支持小型模型的微调（fine-tuning）。
   - 优化推理性能，例如通过改进矩阵乘法操作（matmul operations）。
   - 还有人建议开发WASM版本，以便在浏览器中运行推理。

补充讨论：
• **参考实现和工具**：
   - 项目参考了adriancable/qwen3.c的实现，并通过商业LLM（主要是Claude Sonnet 4）的帮助，将代码从C/Python翻译到Rust。
   - 项目的GitHub链接（https://github.com/reinterpretcat/qwen3-rs）提供了更详细的实现细节和使用说明。

争议焦点：
• **使用unsafe代码的安全性和稳定性**：
   - 虽然unsafe代码可以带来性能上的提升，但也有开发者对其可能引入的安全隐患表示担忧，认为需要在性能和安全性之间找到平衡。

Description
qwen3-rs
is an educational Rust project for exploring and running Qwen3 language family models. It is designed to be clear, modular, and approachable for learners, with minimal dependencies and many core algorithms reimplemented from scratch for transparency.
Note:
Parts of this codebase, including documentation and core algorithms, were generated or assisted by large language models (LLMs) to accelerate development and improve educational clarity. As a starting reference, the project
qwen3.c
was used for understanding model internals and file formats.
Project Goals
Educational:
Learn how transformer architectures, quantization, and efficient inference work in Rust.
Minimal Dependencies:
Most algorithms (tokenization, quantization, sampling, etc.) are implemented from scratch—no heavy ML or Python bindings.
Modular:
Core library logic is separated from CLI tools for clarity and maintainability.
Efficiency:
Uses memory mapping and zero-copy techniques for handling large model files.
Workspace Structure
qwen3-rs/
├── docs                # LLM generated docs for key components
├── Cargo.toml          # Workspace configuration
├── qwen3-cli/          # Command-line interface crate
├── qwen3-export/       # Model export crate
├── qwen3-inference/    # LLM inference crate
How to Use
1. Get a HuggingFace Qwen3 model
git clone https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
#
Or try larger/alternative models:
#
git clone https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B
#
git clone https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B
#
git clone https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B
2. Build and run the exporter
cargo build --release -p qwen3-cli
#
Export a HuggingFace model to quantized checkpoint format
cargo run --release -p qwen3-cli --
export
/path/to/model /path/to/output.bin --group-size 64
3. Run inference
In chat mode with default parameters:
cargo run --release -p qwen3-cli -- inference /path/to/output.bin -m chat
CLI Commands and Options
export
Exports a HuggingFace Qwen3 model to a custom binary format for efficient Rust inference.
Usage:
qwen3

: Path to HuggingFace model directory (must contain config.json, *.safetensors, tokenizer.json)

,

data.title: Doorbell-interceptor: Using a RTL-SDR dongle to receive signals on 433Mhz

doorbell-interceptor
This project uses a Digital TV dongle (RTL-SDR) to receive signals on 433Mhz and post alerts via MQTT.
Background
Whilst my house isn't huge, it can be a struggle to hear the doorbell from the loft room where I've found myself working during lockdown (and beyond).  It's a bog-standard wireless variety from Volex, and I didn't fancy shelling out a fortune for a Ring, and had the technology lying around to try to pick up the signal.
I had intended to use an ESP8266 and a superheterodyne 433Mhz receiver with OpenMQTTGateway for this, but as it turned out, my doorbell doesn't quite transmit on 433.9Mhz like everyone else's, but on 434.0Mhz.
I had an RTL-SDR dongle to hand (which I used to verify the frequency) and was able to use this to pick up the signal.  More of a sledgehammer than the ESP solution but extremely flexible.
I'm using Windows here but all the below is supported on Linux.  I'm definitely standing on the shoulders of giants with the great libraries and resources that are out there.
Requirements
Any RTL-SDR dongle, mostly available for under $10 on Aliexpress or Banggood.
The fantastic RTL_433 from
https://github.com/merbanan/rtl_433
Python 3.x
Paho MQTT Client (
pip install paho-mqtt
)
Optional: SDR# from
https://airspy.com/download/
Discovery
Verify the frequency
Fire up SDR# (you may need to install the relevant drivers for the dongle with Zadig)
Tune to around 433.9Mhz
Send your signal
You should see something like this:
Great, you can see your doorbell signal!
You may need to tune around if you don't see it around 433.9Mhz as I did.
Decode the signal
RTL_433 can analyse the signals being received and produce a general purpose decoder to help pinpoint that signal amongst the others.
Run
rtl_433 -A
to start analysing and press the doorbell.
This should give you an output like this:
This has recognised the signal as being pulse-width modulation, and has calculated the short and long widths of the pulses, and even given us the code we need to produce a flex-decoder!
It also shows the binary code produced by the doorbell.
Let's check the flex decoder by running rtL_433 again with the flex decoder, so in my case:
rtl_433 -X "n=doorbell,m=OOK_PWM,s=372,l=716,r=5356,g=684,t=136,y=0,match={13}0xad08,repeats>=3"
You should see the signals being received with these characteristics, and nothing else - perfect!
Producing MQTT packets
I ended up adapting the code from:
https://github.com/mverleun/RTL433-to-mqtt
As I needed to provide a flex decoder, I ended up putting this into an array for the command and calling this in subprocess.Popen.  I also had to adapt the line that publishes the MQTT packet as it was creating duplicates, but the above code does all the heavy lifting of connecting to the MQTT broker and publishing the signal from RTL433.
Into Node-RED...
I use Node-RED for various bits of home automation and it will happily take an MQTT packet and do something with it.  I use Telegram bots to receive updates on my phone (and send commands back).
...and out to Telegram
There's an awesome and comprehensive Node for Telegram at:
https://flows.nodered.org/node/node-red-contrib-telegrambot
.
There's loads of docs for that so I won't go into detail here, but you'll basically need to use the Sender node and create a function to generate the message:
msg
.
payload
=
{
chatId
:
YOURCHATID
,
type
:
'message'
,
content
:
"There's someone at the door!"
}
return
msg
;
All done!

• mips_avatar 建议通过面对面的方式销售产品，认为这种更脆弱和直接的方式能获得更多回应。

• codingdave 提出应重新联系最初的10个测试用户，通过他们的反馈和口碑传播来获取更多客户。

• vinibrito 认为缺乏网络是主要问题，建议直接与潜在客户交谈。

• mortsmel 分享了自己失败的经验，强调了市场营销和目标客户选择的重要性。他建议通过LinkedIn的高级联系人搜索、广告服务（如Facebook、Google）、以及其他预算较低的广告平台（如vibe.co和caasie.co）来获取客户。他还提到以女性为目标消费者可能是一个有效的策略，并建议加入商会来推销服务。

• bell-cot 指出不同领域的客户需求差异巨大，如企业客户与小企业或学前教育客户的需求截然不同，强调了针对不同市场需要不同的策略。

争议焦点：
• 关于是否依赖人际网络进行营销存在争议。muzani 认为依赖网络是低效的，而 mortsmel 则强调了通过建立关系获取客户的重要性。

• 选择销售渠道和目标市场的策略存在不同看法。muzani 主张多样化渠道，而其他评论者更倾向于面对面销售、口碑传播或通过广告直接触达客户。

整体讨论显示出在寻找产品市场契合度和有效营销策略中的复杂性，以及根据不同市场需求调整策略的必要性。

data.title: Bcachefs Lands Fixes in Linux 6.16 for Some "High Severity" Regressions
data.author: Bender
data.article_summary: 在Linux 6.16-rc6版本发布前，Bcachefs文件系统修复了一些“高严重性”回归问题。Bcachefs的主要开发者Kent Overstreet提交了一个包含多个修复的请求，包括调整b-tree缓存助手、b-tree节点扫描不再使用缓存、修复b-tree读取重试等。这些修复已被Linus Torvalds合并，将在Linux 6.16-rc6中发布。不过，Torvalds尚未明确Bcachefs未来在主线内核中的计划，仅表示在6.17版本中Bcachefs将与主线“分道扬镳”，但未说明是否移除或暂时搁置该文件系统。目前，Bcachefs的修复仍被接受用于Linux 6.16。
