44544996.article_content:
Bcachefs Lands Fixes In Linux 6.16 For Some "High Severity" Regressions
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Linux Storage
on 12 July 2025 at 03:21 PM EDT.
9 Comments
Ahead of tomorrow's Linux 6.16-rc6 kernel release a number of Bcachefs file-system fixes were merged.
On Friday the Bcachefs lead developer Kent Overstreet sent out
a pull request
containing the latest Bcachefs fixes. This includes a number of fixes, tweaking the b-tree cache helpers, b-tree node scans no longer using the cache, b-tree read retry fixes, and various other fixes.
Overstreet followed-up today to the Bcachefs pull request by
noting
:
"These are fixes for some high severity 6.16 regressions."
Linus Torvalds has now merged all of these Bcachefs file-system fixes in time for Sunday's Linux 6.16-rc6 release.
Torvalds hasn't commented any further on what he plans to do about this file-system moving forward. Torvalds commented last month that Bcachefs and the mainline Linux kernel would be
"parting ways in the 6.17 merge window"
without elaborating if he plans to outright remove all the Bcachefs code from the mainline kernel, gate it behind the "BROKEN" Kconfig option, do another time-out for a kernel cycle, or what exactly will happen to this copy-on-write open-source file-system moving forward in the mainline kernel. We'll see but for now Bcachefs fixes are still being accepted for Linux 6.16.

data.title: Million Times Million
data.author: susam
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了长尺度与短尺度两种命名大数的方法。作者在童年时学习的是长尺度系统，其中百万乘以百万是十亿，百万乘以自身三次是万亿，依次类推。每个前缀清晰地表示乘以百万的次数，非常直观。然而，进入大学并接触计算机和互联网后，作者发现短尺度系统更为普遍，在短尺度中，百万乘以百万是万亿，百万乘以三次是 quintillion，这与长尺度差异显著。短尺度通过每增加一千的倍数来命名，例如，从一千开始，每多乘一个一千，就形成更大的单位。尽管短尺度不如长尺度直观，但如今在技术、金融和大多数英语语境中广泛使用。作者最终适应了短尺度，但长尺度的记忆仍留在心中。

主要讨论点：不同数字命名系统（长短尺度）的使用及其带来的困惑和争议

不同观点：
• **长短尺度的历史演变及原因**：danbruc指出，长短尺度的差异源于历史上数字分组方式的变化，从每组六位数变为每组三位数，但命名调整过程中出现了一些不一致，如"trillion"在长尺度下应为"quintillion"。
• **西班牙语中的混用及困惑**：pilaf提到在西班牙语中，长尺度是传统用法，但近年来由于英语和互联网的影响，短尺度用法增多，导致混淆，特别是在新闻等正式场合中使用时会产生歧义。
• **不同语言中的数字系统**：vincnetas和GolDDranks分别提到德语和东亚语言中的数字命名系统，它们各自有不同的分组方式，如东亚语言基于10000的指数系统，这与欧美的千位系统不同。
• **长尺度的优势及普及问题**：eviks认为长尺度更好，因为需要记忆的前缀较少，规则简单，但未解释为何未普及。perilunar则认为极高的数字在实际应用中不常用，科学和工程记数法或SI前缀更为实用。
• **文化及语言差异的影响**：marginalia_nu和dotnetcarpenter提到，在不同语言和文化中，长短尺度及不同单位系统的使用是自然而然的事情，但在翻译和跨文化交流中容易产生混淆。

补充讨论：
• **实际应用中的困惑及误解**：Jotalea分享了作为双语者在西班牙语和英语之间切换时，因长短尺度不同而产生的困惑，如YouTube观看次数表述的不同。
• **对数字系统的改进建议**：user____name建议在计算器程序中加入多语言的长短尺度转换功能，以解决使用中的困惑。
• **历史语言对现代的影响**：OkPin指出短尺度在现代使用中虽然更实用，但从词源上看，长尺度更符合拉丁词根的原意，显示了历史语言对现代的影响。

争议焦点：长短尺度混用导致的歧义和不便，特别是在跨文化交流和翻译中。

Million Times Million
By
Susam Pal
on 03 Jul 2025
Is a million times a million a
billion
or is it
a
trillion
?  For my entire childhood, it was a billion,
only for me to grow up and realise, as an adult, that it had better
be a trillion!
Growing Up With the Long Scale
As a child, I stumbled upon an old dictionary lying around our
house, and that was where I discovered the names of large numbers.
The dictionary used the long scale system, which is based on powers
of a million.  According to the long scale system,
a million times a million is a billion,
a million times a million times a million is a trillion,
a million multiplied by itself four times is a quadrillion,
multiply it five times and we get a quintillion,
and so on.
These long scale names made a lot of sense to me.  Each name told us
exactly how many times we multiplied a million by itself.  The
little prefix at the start, like
bi-
,
tri-
,
quadri-
,
quinti-
, etc.  matched the number of
times a million appeared in the multiplication: twice for a billion,
three times for a trillion, and so on.  If I came across a number
like quintillion, I immediately knew it meant a million multiplied
by itself five times, so a quintillion had to be \( (10^6)^5 =
10^{30}.  \)  It was simple, straightforward, and intuitive!
Now imagine my disappointment when I left home for university, got
access to computers and the World Wide Web, and discovered that the
names I had learnt were off by several orders of magnitude compared
with what everyone else was using.  The long scale names I had grown
up with were irrelevant in this new world I was stepping into.  It
was the short scale that had taken over most of the technology
world, especially in computing.  In the short scale, a million times
a million is no longer a billion.  Instead, somehow, it is a
trillion!  Similarly, a million multiplied three times is no longer
a trillion.  It is a quintillion!  What on earth was going on?
Naturally, I had to go through a period of adjustment, letting go of
my old intuition for the long scale names and getting used to the
short scale ones.  At the same time, I found a way to trick my mind
into making sense of the short scale.  Before I get into the mental
gymnastics that made the short scale click for me, let us first take
a quick look at the long scale and short scale names side by side.
Same Names, Different Numbers
The long scale and short scale are simply two different ways of
naming large numbers.  To see how they differ, here is a table
showing what each name corresponds to in the two systems.
Number
Long Scale
Short Scale
\( 10^6 \)
Million
Million
\( 10^9 \)
Milliard
Billion
\( 10^{12} \)
Billion
Trillion
\( 10^{15} \)
Billiard
Quadrillion
\( 10^{18} \)
Trillion
Quintillion
\( 10^{21} \)
Trilliard

\( 10^{24} \)
Quadrillion

\( 10^{27} \)

\( 10^{33} \)
Quintilliard
Decillion
As the table shows, the two systems agree on the value of a million,
but diverge immediately after.  From that point on, the same names
represent increasingly different magnitudes.
Making Sense of the Short Scale
I used to quite like the long scale names because the prefix in each
name is determined by how many times we multiply a million by
itself.  Each prefix reflects the value of \( n \) in the number \(
10^{6n}, \) where \( n \) is a positive integer.  For example, if \(
n = 3, \) we get \( 10^{18}, \) which in the long scale is called
a
trillion
.  But in the short scale, the same number is
called a
quintillion
.  How can we make sense of it?
One way to interpret the short scale is to count how many additional
thousands are multiplied onto one thousand.  A thousand is, of
course, just
one thousand
.  Multiply it by another thousand
and we get a
million
.  Multiply that by another thousand
and we get a
billion
.  One more multiplication gives us
a
trillion
, and so on.  I do not find this quite as neat as
the long scale but it works!
In effect, the prefix in the short scale corresponds to \( n \) of
the integer \( 1000 \times 1000^n, \) where \( n \) is a positive
integer.  Stated more succinctly, it represents \( n \) of \(
10^{3(n + 1)}.  \)  So for example, if \( n = 5, \) then
\[
10^{3(n + 1)} = 10^{18},
\]
which is called a
quintillion
in the short scale.  The
quinti-
prefix still represents five but now it is tied to
the number of additional thousands we multiplied to the first
thousand.  It is not quite the elegant pattern I grew up with but
this is the convention that dominates today.  In the world of
technology, computing, and finance, as well as in most
English-speaking contexts, the short scale has prevailed.
Conclusion
Today, of course, I use only the short scale, because that is the
convention adopted by the part of the world relevant to me.  I no
longer use the long scale.  But it remains in memory, simply because
I spent a large part of my early life with it.  It still lives in

• **长短尺度的历史演变及原因**：danbruc指出，长短尺度的差异源于历史上数字分组方式的变化，从每组六位数变为每组三位数，但命名调整过程中出现了一些不一致，如"trillion"在长尺度下应为"quintillion"。
• **西班牙语中的混用及困惑**：pilaf提到在西班牙语中，长尺度是传统用法，但近年来由于英语和互联网的影响，短尺度用法增多，导致混淆，特别是在新闻等正式场合中使用时会产生歧义。
• **不同语言中的数字系统**：vincnetas和GolDDranks分别提到德语和东亚语言中的数字命名系统，它们各自有不同的分组方式，如东亚语言基于10000的指数系统，这与欧美的千位系统不同。
• **长尺度的优势及普及问题**：eviks认为长尺度更好，因为需要记忆的前缀较少，规则简单，但未解释为何未普及。perilunar则认为极高的数字在实际应用中不常用，科学和工程记数法或SI前缀更为实用。
• **文化及语言差异的影响**：marginalia_nu和dotnetcarpenter提到，在不同语言和文化中，长短尺度及不同单位系统的使用是自然而然的事情，但在翻译和跨文化交流中容易产生混淆。

补充讨论：
• **实际应用中的困惑及误解**：Jotalea分享了作为双语者在西班牙语和英语之间切换时，因长短尺度不同而产生的困惑，如YouTube观看次数表述的不同。
• **对数字系统的改进建议**：user____name建议在计算器程序中加入多语言的长短尺度转换功能，以解决使用中的困惑。
• **历史语言对现代的影响**：OkPin指出短尺度在现代使用中虽然更实用，但从词源上看，长尺度更符合拉丁词根的原意，显示了历史语言对现代的影响。

争议焦点：长短尺度混用导致的歧义和不便，特别是在跨文化交流和翻译中。

Tony Tyson’s cameras revealed the universe’s dark contents. Now, with the Rubin Observatory’s 3.2-billion-pixel camera, he’s ready to study dark matter and dark energy in unprecedented detail.

On June 23, 2025, Tony Tyson joined a presentation in Washington, D.C., to unveil an image almost 30 years in the making: 10 million galaxies poised on an inky black backdrop. To appreciate each galaxy in detail, you’d have to stretch the picture across 400 TVs. It’s the first portrait of the cosmos delivered by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, a new astronomical facility built by the United States on a mountain in Chile. And it captures just 0.05% of the galaxies that the observatory’s mammoth camera will record over the next decade.
That camera is ushering in an ultra-vivid new era of astronomy; it’s also Tyson’s magnum opus.
Tyson, a cosmologist at the University of California, Davis and the chief scientist of the Rubin Observatory, was working at Bell Labs in the 1970s when he encountered a novel imaging chip called a charge-coupled device (CCD) and realized that it could revolutionize the study of the universe. By converting incoming light into electrical signals, CCD sensors are well suited for detecting faint, distant objects in the cosmos. Tyson used the technology to make
the first high-resolution map of dark matter
, the mysterious, heavy substance that binds galaxies together like an invisible glue.
Then, in the 1990s, other astronomers used one of Tyson’s CCD cameras to study the expansion of the universe and discovered what seemed like a mistake at the time: The expansion was ramping up. The peculiar acceleration revealed the presence of dark energy.
Today, dark matter and dark energy — together composing 95% of the contents of the universe — remain utter mysteries. Even in the 1990s, Tyson knew that to illuminate these dark entities, he’d need to study them with a bigger camera, so he founded the project that has become the Rubin Observatory. Now 85, he is finally introducing his brainchild to the world.
An array of 189 CCDs totaling 3.2 billion pixels, the Rubin Observatory’s Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) camera is the largest digital camera ever built. Over the next 10 years, it will repeatedly photograph approximately 20 billion galaxies. Among other things, the photo album will chronicle the convoluted history of how dark matter and dark energy conspired to carve out the structure of our universe.

Can you walk me through how you created a map of dark matter?
I was always interested, even as a kid, in measuring things that were almost undetectable — really, really faint signals, first in the radio and then optical wavelengths. Bell Labs gave me free rein to engineer new systems that would detect those extremely faint signals. One day, George Smith [co-inventer of the charge-coupled device] came into my office and said, “You know, with your interest in astronomy, you might be interested in this.” It was this little thing that was a couple millimeters long, known nowadays as a CCD.
At the time, I was really interested in how galaxies look like they’ve been moved by all of this invisible dark matter in between us and them. The galaxy’s light gets distorted by the gravity of the dark matter, so the image of the galaxy becomes elongated, turning into a little arc. So I developed a very simple detector with CCDs that looks for this telltale arc-iness around the sky. The term is called weak gravitational lensing. When you detect the mirage, you can invert the map to see the distribution of the dark matter.

data.title: Switching to Claude Code and VSCode Inside Docker
data.author: timsh
data.article_summary: 作者分享了从旧的AI编码设置（使用ChatGPT Plus和Cursor Pro）切换到在Docker中运行Claude Code的经历，并提供了简要指南和代码链接。他提到之前设置的问题包括Cursor Pro的响应缓慢和新的请求限制不合理，以及对AI代理安全性的担忧，特别是它们能访问整个文件系统和终端。为解决这些问题，作者选择使用Claude的20美元订阅，并通过Docker容器限制其访问权限，以提高安全性。这种方法让他能以更低的成本获得更好的编码体验，同时确保系统安全。作者提供了详细的操作指南和代码，供其他有类似需求的用户参考。

44533044.article_content:
Last night I finished a transition from my old AI coding setup I've been using for a while to running Claude Code in Docker using VSCode's "Dev Container" feature.
In this post I lay out a few of my thoughts on why I wanted to switch to something in the first place, and also a short guide for those who want to do the same.
If you are here just for the guide + code (a tiny single file), here it is:
https://github.com/tim-sha256/claude-in-docker
🥺
Important note!
I'm not a professional vibecoder (thanks god) and I don't generate AI code on 9-5 basis (meh)
I'm just a casual user occasionally getting help from llms on my projects, all of them being not corporate-serious-guys-enterprise-grade.
I'm not looking for the most advanced 100x dev tools or workflows, nor $100+ subscriptions whose token limits I'll probably only reach once a year on a sleepless night.
Before and why
Until yesterday I've been using such setup:
ChatGPT Plus 20$ subscription for occasional chats mostly unrelated to code, except for quickies and desperate attempts to feed o3 a bunch of code that Claude can't crack and get it all solved (mostly unsuccessful).
Cursor Pro for additional 20$ (or how do they call it these days?) - for all "serious" coding.
Which works all right, is convenient (been stuck with Cursor since August '24 and GPT since '23 without actively seeking an alternative), but has a couple issues that started to bug me recently.
Issue 1: I'm greedy and I want my responses fast
Before Cursor went into drain-users stage recently, I did not use up all 500 requests / month not a single time while working on 1-2 projects during my free time (approx. 40-60 hours a month).
Maybe I could've paid less on token-based plan, but I didn't really care – $20 is $20 :)
But after their update removing the 500 requests limit "so you can enjoy unlimited requests to almost any model", I've been extremely upset by Cursor due to their inadequate rate limits.
Sometimes I would type a prompt for Sonnet 4 (not even Opus...) and wait for 2-5 minutes for anything to happen, which is a complaint I've seen quite a lot in Cursor-related chats and on Reddit.
There is an option to switch back to a proprietary and seemingly not as profitable 500 requests pricing mode, but I don't think it'll last much longer.  Or use the free version and go out for a smoke break after every request.
Which led me to think about my spending and the satisfaction I get in return: is it still worth 40$ or is there a better way?
Well, for now I've settled with Claude 20$ subscription and consider it a better fit for my use case for a couple of reasons:
$20 is less than 40$
I still get to send a pic of a shelf with various cleaning products to some chat app on my phone and ask "Which of these do I need to do X?", which works surprisingly well almost all the time
I have a similar-or-even-better web chat experience to work on stuff unrelated to code
Finally, and most importantly – I get Claude Code with:
reasonable limits
clear token spending indication
everybody constantly says Claude Code rocks, right?
I like cli stuff in general
vs code integration makes the IDE experience essentially the same (or even a bit better)
Ok, looks like I'm settled for now, end of story. Or what else?
Issue 2: I'm trying to be realistic about AI Agent security
Simply put: I believe running an AI Agent that has access to your entire file system, terminal and secrets is dangerous and will eventually lead to some problems.
Think of it as if you gave access to your computer to a cheap overseas freelance dev who you don't really know and can only chat with. How does that sound?
I stumble upon llm security-related stuff every day and occasionally read some of it. And generally, the situation is not getting better.
For instance, I've seen around 10 posts about very serious vulnerabilities in MCPs like
this one,
a few sad stories where cursor decided to delete something useful like all Ableton projects using
rm -rf
, and even threads saying that Claude
learned to bypass Cursor built-in command blacklist
in Yolo mode.
Basically, you have a choice: either accept each single command manually (which I think is a reasonable approach but I'm too lazy) or trust the above mentioned freelancer with everything you have and hope that some barriers will stop it and nothing bad will happen.
Or are there any other options?
Now and why
Ok, so I want to use Claude Code, but at the same time want to restrict it somehow so it can't fuck up my entire computer.
First idea which came to me turned to be the one that I'd go with (who could've thought): put that thing into a box with nothing but the project(s) in it, give it the least possible access and close the box.
In other words, launch Claude Code in Docker and work on the project inside the container.
What you get from that:
Claude can only access files from inside the container or in the provided volumes, mounted or not
It also most certainly can't break anything outside the con

data.title: Chrome's hidden X-Browser-Validation header reverse engineered
data.author: dsekz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个针对Chrome浏览器私有头部"x-browser-validation"的反向工程与生成工具。该头部用于完整性验证，确保用户代理与平台匹配，防止伪造。该头部通过连接平台特定的API密钥和用户代理字符串，使用SHA-1算法进行哈希，然后进行Base64编码生成。文章提供了生成该头部的Python代码示例，并详细描述了反向工程过程，包括在Chrome二进制文件中找到相关函数和算法。最终确认该头部的生成过程为：API密钥 + 用户代理字符串 → SHA-1哈希 → Base64编码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Chrome浏览器中新增的"x-browser-validation" header的目的及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• [技术分析与用途猜测]  
  - [dsekz] 分析了chrome.dll并弄清了"x-browser-validation" header的生成方式，提到这可能与反欺诈、机器人检测或完整性验证有关。

Chrome X-Browser-Validation Header Reverse Engineering & Generator
Chrome recently added a few new headers:
"x-browser-channel": "stable",
"x-browser-copyright": "Copyright 2025 Google LLC. All rights reserved.",
"x-browser-validation": "6h3XF8YcD8syi2FF2BbuE2KllQo=",
"x-browser-year": "2025"
Apart from one of them, there isn’t much that’s interesting. They’re just bits of client specific information. However, base64 decoding x-browser-validation yields what appears to be a hash whose purpose remains undocumented.
Chrome almost certainly uses this header as an integrity signal. Verifying that the declared user agent matches the underlying platform, spotting user agent string spoofing attempts etc.
Generator

generate_validation_header

A hard-coded, platform specific API key

Concatenate

Hash

with SHA-1 and base64 encode it.

Opened
chrome.dll
in IDA. The master routine
sub_1806C95B0
builds every
X-Browser-*
header (you can find this function by searching
browser-validation
etc):
Data prep - grabs the first hard-coded API key for the OS and appends the full user agent.

v46

*

v30
=
"X-Browser-Validation"
;
sub_183C6B920
(

}
Hash - passes that buffer into
sub_183B509D0
, which is SHA-1 algo. Open this guy and the first assignment jumps out:
v12
[
0
]
=
xmmword_7FFE2C9A7D50

The second you see that "-1009589776" number, you can literally smell SHA-1.
Base64 - the 20-byte digest is encoded.
Dynamic confirmation: pause one instruction before the hash call, dump RDX, and the ~150-byte buffer is nothing but
<API_KEY><User-Agent>
Base64(SHA-1(buffer)) = header. Mystery solved.

data.title: Hacking Coroutines into C
data.author: jmillikin
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在一个嵌入式软件项目中，如何通过将协程概念引入C语言来简化状态机的实现。传统的状态机方法在处理多个状态和事件时，代码难以维护和理解。作者受高级语言中协程的启发，提出了一种在不使用操作系统的情况下实现类似协程的并发处理方法。文章通过一个LED闪烁控制和按钮按下时间记录的例子，展示了如何用状态机和轮询机制实现功能。虽然这种方法可行，但代码复杂且不易读。作者建议引入类似协程的机制，以简化逻辑流和状态管理，从而提高代码的可读性和可维护性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C语言中实现轻量级协程和状态机的不同方法及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持使用Protothreads和宏实现协程**：
   - [adinisom] 支持使用Protothreads，通过简单的宏和结构体实现协程，认为这种方式能很好地结合声明式和过程式代码，并且在实际硬件中有效。
   - 例子：提供了具体的代码示例，展示了如何通过`YIELD()`宏和`switch`语句实现协程。

• **质疑状态机和协程的复杂性**：
   - [astrobe_] 认为状态机缺乏线性流程，使用状态机是因为控制流不线性，但这种方式可能不如`goto`清晰。同时指出，状态机的可视化和模块化是难题。
   - 提出并发和非线性问题的不同解决方式，认为试图同时解决两个问题可能导致不良后果。

• **建议使用实时操作系统（RTOS）或代码生成工具**：
   - [mikepurvis] 提到FreeRTOS可以实现协作式调度，并建议使用代码生成工具来提高可读性和正确性检查。
   - [userbinator] 指出在没有RTOS的项目中，最终可能会实现一个近似的方案，并建议使用PWM外设或定时器中断以简化实现。

• **提供替代方案和批评复杂性**：
   - [codr7] 认为所展示的实现过于复杂，提供了一个替代方案的链接。
   - [user____name] 认为在C语言中模拟协程过于复杂，建议语言级别支持协程，否则可能得不偿失。

• **其他实现方式和历史视角**：
   - [syncurrent] 提到基于Esterel或Blech的同步语言的实现方式，并提供了一个链接。
   - [Neywiny] 不喜欢在软件中使用状态机，认为它们在FPGA/ASIC中更合适，并支持函数的线性执行。
   - [moconnor] 提到通过手动更新栈和跳转实现协程的旧方法，指出这种方法已有几十年的历史。

• **简短评论和提及其他技术**：
   - [throwaway81523] 认为展示的实现类似于多年前的protothreads，并批评文章的CSS设计。
   - [joshlk] 提到Rust在嵌入式环境中的应用，提供了一种内建异步执行的现代语言选择。
   - [Nursie] 认为使用`setjmp`和`longjmp`的协程实现是C语言中的一种古老技术，可能正在逐渐被遗忘。

补充讨论：
• **可视化和工具支持**：
   - [astrobe_] 强调了可视化工具的重要性，并提到Pharo的检查工具可以帮助理解底层运行情况。
   - 提出了一种理想工具的设想，能够通过节点和箭头表示状态机，并生成文本中间语言以兼容Git。

争议焦点：
• 状态机和协程在C语言中的实现是否过于复杂，是否有更好的替代方案（如使用RTOS或现代语言如Rust）。
• 使用宏和手动跳转等技术是否比现代代码生成工具和高级语言特性更有效。

主要讨论点：租车公司（尤其是Hertz）在处理归还车辆时的费用争议和流程问题

不同观点：
• **流程不透明和事后收费不合理**：[remram] 认为，归还车辆时，如果工作人员没有当场指出损坏，而事后收到账单，这种做法不合理。应该在归还时立即扫描车辆并当场结账。
• **现行流程的缺陷**：[legitster] 指出当前流程存在缺陷，检查人员培训不足，且检查不够严谨，但认为Hertz并非故意不公，流程至少是透明的。
• **保险和额外收费的目的**：[pseudolus] 和 [t1234s] 认为，租车公司通过高额保险（如碰撞损坏险）来增加收入，目的是让租客购买更多保险，从而增加租车成本。
• **Hertz品牌形象的衰退**：[alwa] 和 [kjellsbells] 提到Hertz曾经是 prestige brand，但目前品牌形象不佳，存在财务问题和管理混乱，甚至存在敲诈消费者的行为。
• **未来竞争和流程改善**：[benced] 认为，随着市场竞争和公众关注，流程会逐渐改善，变得更合理。
• **旅行保险的替代作用**：[boznz] 建议在国外租车时，可以通过旅行保险覆盖超额费用，这样可以避免购买昂贵的租车保险。
• **Hertz的法律和信誉问题**：[kevingadd] 引用了Hertz错误指控客户盗窃的案例，认为不应该与Hertz交易，并建议购买全险以避免麻烦。

补充讨论：
• **对新技术的担忧和抵制**：[schrodinger] 提出一种极端假设，即在扫描前后故意损坏车辆以测试系统如何处理，暗示对新技术的担忧。[eggn00dles] 则认为这是公司在测试公众对新技术的反应。

data.title: Most (ly Dead) Influential Programming Languages (2020)
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了历史上具有重大影响的编程语言，批评了一份忽略了如ALGOL、Smalltalk和ML等重要语言的榜单。文章强调了一些“几乎消亡”但对计算历史有重大影响的编程语言，如COBOL和ALGOL。作者解释了如何通过引用链和编程语言的相似性来判断语言的影响力。文章详细介绍了COBOL和ALGOL的历史背景、重要性及其消亡原因。COBOL引入了记录数据概念，但对后续语言影响有限；ALGOL尽管几乎消亡，但对现代编程语言的许多特性有深远影响。文章提醒读者历史复杂，调查可能有误。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言的现状及其是否被视为“死亡”或“几乎死亡”

不同观点：
• **addaon的观点**：addaon认为Self语言应被更多关注。他指出Self不仅直接影响了Smalltalk，还在JIT（即时编译）研究和原型继承的对象系统方面有重要影响，尤其是对JavaScript的对象模型有直接影响。addaon强调了Self语言的历史和技术贡献，认为其被忽视是不妥的。

• **alwinw的观点**：alwinw对“几乎死亡”的定义表示好奇，并提出一些语言（如COBOL）虽然在大多数领域不再广泛使用，但在特定领域（如银行业的COBOL）仍然活跃。alwinw质疑如果一种语言不再更新、没有新包开发，是否就可以被认为是“几乎死亡”，表明对语言生命周期定义的疑惑。

• **Rochus的观点**：Rochus直接反驳将COBOL视为“死亡”或“几乎死亡”的说法。他通过引用具体数据（如COBOL处理全球70%的商业交易，且代码量仍在增长）来证明COBOL仍然在实际应用中占有重要地位，不应被轻易视为死亡语言。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：各方对于某些编程语言是否“死亡”或“几乎死亡”的定义和标准有不同看法。alwinw质疑如何定义语言的“死亡”，而Rochus则用数据证明COBOL在实际应用中的活力，反驳其“死亡”的说法。

• **技术影响与实际应用**：addaon强调了Self语言在技术发展中的重要性，尤其是在原型继承和JIT研究上的贡献，而Rochus则通过实际应用数据展示了COBOL在现代商业中的不可或缺性。这些讨论都指向了某些老旧语言在技术发展史和实际应用中的重要作用。

44545050.article_content:
The other day I read
20 most significant programming languages in history
, a “preposterous table I just made up.” He certainly got preposterous right: he lists Go as “most significant” but not ALGOL, Smalltalk, or ML. He also leaves off Pascal because it’s “mostly dead”. Preposterous! That defeats the whole point of what “significant in history” means.
So let’s talk about some “mostly dead” languages and why they matter so much.
Disclaimer:
Yeah not all of these are dead and not all of these are forgotten. Like most people have heard of Smalltalk, right? Also there’s probably like a billion mistakes in this, because when you’re doing a survey of 60 years of computing history you’re gonna get some things wrong. Feel free to yell at me if you see anything!
Disclaimer 2:
Yeah I know some of these are “first to invent” and others are “first to popularize”. History is complicated!
Detecting Influence
Before we start, a quick primer on finding influence. Just knowing that X was the first language with feature Z doesn’t mean that X actually
influenced
Z. While
Absys
was arguably the first logic programming language, almost all of logic programming actually stems from Prolog, which was developed independently. Ultimately there’s only one way to know for certain that X influenced Y: citation. This means one of
Y cites X in its reference manual
Y cites a paper that cites X
The author of Y says “we were influenced by X.”
Citations are transitive. Sometimes the language manual for Q lists motivating document R, which cites paper S as an inspiration, which mentions it got the ideas from language T. Then we know that T influenced Q, even if the chain is several steps long. This means digging through many sources to find a signal. To speed this up we use heuristics to decide where to look.
One effective heuristic is programming language
cognates
. It’s very rare for languages to independently come up with the same syntax. So if two languages share some syntax, one likely influenced the other. For example: even without reading design decisions by Matz, we know that Ruby was influenced by Smalltalk, as they both filter a list with a
select
method. This isn’t conclusive evidence. Maybe Matz came up with it independently, or maybe Ruby and Smalltalk were both influenced by a common ancestor. But it gives us a place to start looking.
The Languages
COBOL
Background:
CODASYL, 1960. COBOL is shaped by the business/science split in computing. At that time high-level industry languages were either used for engineering computations or managing data. The engineers had all gotten behind FORTRAN while the business world was a mess of COMTRAN, FLOW-MATIC, and others, so the Department of Defense got a committee together to make a single universal business language. That’s COBOL.
COBOL was one of the four “mother” languages, along with ALGOL, FORTRAN, and LISP. While we consider it a punchline today, it was once the most popular language in the world. It still runs a lot of our legacy business systems.
Significance
: In terms of syntax and semantics we don’t see much of COBOL in modern computing. COBOL’s most important addition is the concept of record data. In FORTRAN and ALGOL, your only data structure was the static array. In COBOL, though, you could read in structured files with hierarchical data, and it would automatically destructure them into the representative variables. This was a precursor to modern day structs.
Cause of Death
: Two factors here. One: COBOL had no overlap with other PLT efforts. Very few people built on COBOL. This meant that second or third generation languages, which built on the lessons of their ancestors, had almost no COBOL DNA. This was less intrinsic problem of COBOL and more because of the academia’s disdain for its creation process. CODASYL was a business group and obviously wasn’t worth paying attention to.
1
COBOL was also enormously complex, even for today’s languages. This means that COBOL compilers lagged contemporaries on microcomputers and minicomputers, giving spaces for other languages to flourish and eventually outcompete it.
ALGOL
Background
: The ALGOL committee, 1960. ALGOL-58 came out two years before but was quickly superseded, so I’m wrapping them into each other. The committee wanted to make a good language for researching algorithms. In other words, ALGOL was a formalized “pseudocode”.
Of the four mother languages, ALGOL is the most “dead”; Everybody still knows about LISP,
2
COBOL still powers tons of legacy systems, and most scientific packages still have some FORTRAN. But I’ve met plenty of programmers who haven’t even heard of ALGOL. You’d think it’d be the least important of the mother languages, but it’s the opposite. Of the four, only LISP comes anywhere
close
to the pervasive importance of ALGOL.
Significance
: Let’s see: lexical scoping, structured programming, nested functions, formal language specifications, call-by-name semantics, BNF grammars, block comments… every moder

data.title: Startup just hit a big milestone for green steel production
data.author: ohjeez
data.article_summary: Boston Metal，一家致力于生产绿色钢铁的初创公司，近日成功运行其最大反应炉，生产出超过一吨的钢铁，向商业化迈出了重要一步。该公司的技术使用电流通过熔融氧化物电解（MOE）工艺，从铁矿石中提取铁，过程中排放氧气而非二氧化碳，从而大幅减少钢铁生产的温室气体排放。若使用可再生能源供电，该工艺几乎可以实现零排放。尽管距离大规模应用还有许多挑战，但此次成功展示了其技术可扩展性，未来有望改变钢铁行业的高污染现状。

44546533.article_content:
This article is from The Spark,
MIT Technology Review
’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday,
sign up here
.
Green-steel startup Boston Metal just showed that it has all the ingredients needed to make steel without emitting gobs of greenhouse gases. The company successfully ran its largest reactor yet to make steel, producing over a ton of metal,
MIT Technology Review
can exclusively report.
Related Story
The world’s first industrial-scale plant for green steel promises a cleaner future
The Swedish startup Stegra has raised close to $7 billion to produce zero-emissions steel using green hydrogen starting in 2026.
The latest milestone means that Boston Metal just got one step closer to commercializing its technology. The company’s process uses electricity to make steel, and depending on the source of that electricity, it could mean cleaning up production of one of the most polluting materials on the planet. The world produces about 2 billion metric tons of steel each year, emitting over 3 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide in the process.
While there are still a lot of milestones left before reaching the scale needed to make a dent in the steel industry, the latest run shows that the company can scale up its process.
Boston Metal started up its industrial reactor for steelmaking in January, and after it had run for several weeks, the company siphoned out roughly a ton of material on February 17. (You can see a
video of the molten metal here
. It’s really cool.)
Work on this reactor has been underway for a while. I got to visit the facility in Woburn, Massachusetts, in 2022, when construction was nearly done. In the years since, the company has been working on testing it out to make other metals before retrofitting it for steel production.
Boston Metal’s approach is very different from that of a conventional steel plant. Steelmaking typically involves a blast furnace, which uses a coal-based fuel called coke to drive the reactions needed to turn iron ore into iron (the key ingredient in steel). The carbon in coke combines with oxygen pulled out of the iron ore, which gets released as carbon dioxide.
Instead, Boston Metal uses electricity in a process called molten oxide electrolysis (MOE). Iron ore gets loaded into a reactor, mixed with other ingredients, and then electricity is run through it, heating the mixture to around 1,600 °C (2,900 °F) and driving the reactions needed to make iron. That iron can then be turned into steel.
Crucially for the climate, this process emits oxygen rather than carbon dioxide (that infamous greenhouse gas). If renewables like wind and solar or nuclear power are used as the source of electricity, then this approach can virtually cut out the climate impact from steel production.
MOE was developed at MIT, and Boston Metal was founded in 2013 to commercialize the technology. Since then, the company has worked to take it from lab scale, with reactors roughly the size of a coffee cup, to much larger ones that can produce tons of metal at a time. That’s crucial for an industry that operates on the scale of billions of tons per year.
“The volumes of steel everywhere around us—it’s immense,” says Adam Rauwerdink, senior vice president of business development at Boston Metal. “The scale is massive.”
BOSTON METAL
Making the huge amounts of steel required to be commercially relevant has been quite the technical challenge.
One key component of Boston Metal’s design is the anode. It’s basically a rounded metallic bit that sticks into the reactor, providing a way for electricity to get in and drive the reactions required. In theory, this anode doesn’t get used up, but if the conditions aren’t quite right, it can degrade over time.
Over the past few years, the company has made a lot of progress in preventing inert anode degradation, Rauwerdink says. The latest phase of work is more complicated, because now the company is adding multiple anodes in the same reactor.
In lab-scale reactors, there’s one anode, and it’s quite small. Larger reactors require bigger anodes, and at a certain point it’s necessary to add more of them. The latest run continues to prove how Boston Metal’s approach can scale, Rauwerdink says: making reactors larger, adding more anodes, and then adding multiple reactors together in a single plant to make the volumes of material needed.
Related Story
Green steel: 10 Breakthrough Technologies 2025
Making steel produces a lot of greenhouse-gas emissions. Now, construction is underway in Sweden on an industrial-scale plant that will emit almost zero carbon dioxide.
Now that the company has completed its first run of the multi-anode reactor for steelmaking, the plan is to keep exploring how the reactions happen at this larger scale. These runs will also help the company better understand what it will cost to make its products.
The next step is to build an even bigger system, Rauwerdink says—something that won’t fit in the Boston facility. Whi
44546533.article_summary: Boston Metal，一家致力于生产绿色钢铁的初创公司，近日成功运行其最大反应炉，生产出超过一吨的钢铁，向商业化迈出了重要一步。该公司的技术使用电流通过熔融氧化物电解（MOE）工艺，从铁矿石中提取铁，过程中排放氧气而非二氧化碳，从而大幅减少钢铁生产的温室气体排放。若使用可再生能源供电，该工艺几乎可以实现零排放。尽管距离大规模应用还有许多挑战，但此次成功展示了其技术可扩展性，未来有望改变钢铁行业的高污染现状。

data.article_summary: 一架载有260人的 Air India 航班在艾哈迈达巴德起飞后不久坠毁，初步报告显示，坠机前发动机燃料开关处于关闭位置。驾驶舱录音显示，两名飞行员对燃料切断原因存在 confusion。印度航空部长呼吁不要急于下结论，美国航空监管机构表示调查将“遵循事实”。遇难者家属要求真相和正义，有些人对报告未提供明确答案表示不满。印度飞机事故调查局正在调查，最终报告将于明年发布。航空律师指出，初步报告结果令人担忧，需进一步调查以确定事故原因。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：印度航空事故中燃料切断开关的操作及其可能原因

不同观点：
• [SAI_Peregrinus] 认为，如果这是蓄意行为而非失误或故障，那么美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）关于撤销寻求心理健康治疗的飞行员执照的政策是极为不利的。该政策迫使飞行员在职业和治疗之间做出选择，从而鼓励了隐瞒心理健康问题。他提到《2025年航空心理健康法》（HR 2591）正在审议，希望该法案能够通过并影响其他国家改变相关政策。

• [yason] 关注飞行员在短时间内识别出燃料切断开关被触动的可能性。他认为在众多警告和错误信息中，飞行员很难迅速判断出问题所在，并质疑为什么第一个发现问题的飞行员没有立即将开关拨回“运行”位置，而是与其他飞行员讨论。

• [fsckboy] 提出一种可能性，即飞行员在试图收起起落架时因肌肉记忆错误而误触了燃料切断开关。这种解释与驾驶舱对话和起落架未收回的事实相符。

• [bigtones] 引用了专家的观点，指出每个787飞机的燃料开关都配有锁定机制，防止误操作。要将燃料供应打开，开关必须被拉出并移动到“运行”位置，这一过程需要有意识的操作。

• [maxbond] 强调飞行员的英雄行为比飞行员导致的灾难更为常见，并举了几个历史上飞行员成功处理紧急情况的例子，如英国航空5390和联合航空232事件。

• [arctics] 提到油门控制模块在2019年和2023年两次更换，这不常见。结合飞行员的经验，他猜测要么是飞行员故意为之，要么是控制单元故障。

• [melenaboija] 质疑为什么在起飞时有可能切断燃料，并询问是否应该有一个完全禁止这种操作的控制机制。

补充讨论：
• [richardatlarge] 指出不同解释在单独看时似乎都有道理，但当综合考虑时会发现其中的复杂性。
• [nottorp] 提到评论中缺乏对参考链接（avherald）的引用，这可能对理解事件背景有所帮助。
• [bob1029] 提到F-16的紧急动力装置（EPU）可以在极短时间内启动，并认为这对罕见事件有参考价值。
• [jeswin] 提供了一个不同的观点链接，指出四位印度飞行员对报告的怀疑态度，并提到可能有未公开的驾驶舱对话。
• [testemailfordg2] 综合三点分析：1) 飞行员明确表示未进行操作，2) 报告中提到第二个开关在一秒内被关闭，3) 已知开关误触的警告，认为开关操作可能并非人为引起。
• [resist_futility] 提供了一个视频短链接，显示飞行员将燃料切断开关拨回运行位置，进一步复杂化了讨论。

争议焦点：事故中燃料切断开关的操作是否为故意行为，或是否存在设计或操作失误导致误触的可能性。各方对飞行员的行为和飞机设计的安全性存在不同看法。

44536459.article_content:
Summary
A preliminary report on the Air India crash
that killed 260 people finds that both fuel switches were in
the cut-off position
moments before the plane crashed in Ahmedabad
Audio recordings from the cockpit suggest there was confusion between the two pilots over how fuel to the engines cut off -
here's what was said
The audio
only deepens the mystery surrounding the crash
, the BBC's India correspondent Soutik Biswas writes
Grieving families and friends of the victims are mourning their loved ones and demand answers -
here's what we've heard
A spokesperson for Air India says the airline
continues to "fully co-operate" with authorities
-
we've taken a look at what happens next
Media caption,
Watch: What we know about the fuel switches on Air India flight 171
Live Reporting
Edited by Matt Spivey
Imogen James
Live reporter
Image source,
Reuters
Late on Friday night, a preliminary report was released on the Air India crash that killed 260 people on 12 June shortly after take-off in Ahmedabad.
It drew no conclusions, but found that the fuel switches - which turn the engines on and off - were in
the cut-off position
moments before the plane crashed.
Voice recordings from the cockpit reveal that there was confusion between the two pilots over how the switches were cut off. One of the pilots is heard asking the other why he cut them off, the other pilot responds that he did not do so.
India's aviation minister has urged people not to jump to conclusions, as a US aviation watchdog says the investigation will "follow the facts".
Families of some of the victims have been demanding answers. One man tells the BBC he has been left with more questions than answers following the release of the report.
The investigation led by Indiaâs Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, with assistance from the US National Transportation Safety Board, continues.
A final report is due to be released next year.
We're now bringing our live coverage to a close, but you can keep up to date with
everything we know
and read more about
why the cockpit audio deepens the mystery of Air India crash
.

Ayushi Christian's husband Lawrence was killed in the crash last month
In the hours after the preliminary report on the Air India crash was released, we've been hearing from the families and friends of some of the 260 people killed.
'Justice should be served':
Ayushi Christian's husband Lawrence Christian was killed in the crash, she calls for justice for the victims. "Action should be taken against those responsible," she tells the BBC.
'Her story will live on':
The cousin of Lamnunthem Singson, a crew member who lost their life, says the family are "trying to make sense of our loss". He explains that he is not sure if knowing the reason for the crash will change the way they are grieving.
'Was it avoidable?':
Badasab Syed, 59, lost his brother, sister-in-law and their two children in the crash. He says he was left with more questions than answers following the release of the report.
'Did he suffer when he died?':
Shweta Parihar lost her husband Abhinav Parihar in the aviation disaster, she says the ongoing investigation offers her little comfort. "What is the point of the investigation now? We are finished,â she tells the BBC.
'We don't have words to describe our pain':
Rafiq Dawood's 25-year-old son, Faizan Rafiq, died in the crash. "We don't know about the fuel switch or other technical details. The fact is that we have lost our son," he says.
'Our hopes have been shattered':
A relative of Saiyed Javed Ali, who died in the crash along with his wife and two children, has called on the Indian government to act against those responsible. "Proper investigation should be done to find what caused the crash," he says.
Image source,
RAFIQ MEMON
Image caption,
Saiyed Javed Ali, his wife and two children were killed in the crash

close panel

About sharing
An aviation lawyer, who is advising some of the grieving families, says the findings of the initial report in to the Air India crash are "deeply concerning".
Demitrus Danas, from British firm Irwin Mitchell, says the findings "certainly merit further scrutiny to establish the full facts around how this tragedy happened".
âWeâre continuing to speak with and advise families whoâve been affected by the Air India crash. Understandably, all they want is to be provided with answers," he adds in a statement.
âAs investigations continue, weâd urge families not to feel pressured by Air Indiaâs owners into signing documents relating to potential compensation payments."

data.title: Banned Filipino fishermen documentary can be seen in NZ
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: 菲律宾导演Baby Ruth Villarama的纪录片《Food Delivery, Fresh from the West Philippine Sea》在被菲律宾主要电影节撤下后，在新西兰的Doc Edge电影节上成功放映。该片记录了菲律宾渔民在中国海警监控下在争议海域捕鱼的故事。中国驻奥克兰总领事馆曾要求Doc Edge不要放映此片，称其传播虚假信息和政治宣传，但Doc Edge拒绝了这一要求，坚持放映。Villarama对Doc Edge的支持表示感谢，她强调拍摄过程艰辛且未受政府资助，旨在为渔民发声，展现他们在主权争议和资源争夺中的困境。她呼吁人们关注自然资源的保护和共享。

44546583.article_content:
Banned Filipino fishermen documentary can be seen in NZ
Doc Edge has screened the documentary, despite a request from the Consulate-General of China in Auckland to not do so.
Nine To Noon
6 min read
Nine To Noon
6 min read
Caption:
A picture from the documentary 'Food Delivery, Fresh from the West Philippine Sea'.
Photo credit:
Supplied / Elephant Publicity
Top filmmaker Baby Ruth Villarama, whose new documentary was pulled from the Philippine's major film festival, says she’s grateful
Doc Edge
stood by its decision to screen the film despite a request from the Consulate-General of China.
In
Food Delivery, Fresh from the West Philippine Sea
, she follows a group of fishers from a small village as they navigate their fishing grounds, while keeping a wary eye for the Chinese coastguard.
This area of the ocean has long been a flashpoint for relations between the Philippines and China, which both claim territorial ownership for it. That's despite
China's loss in a 2016 ruling
at the Permanent Court of Arbitration.
Play video
Pause video
This video is hosted on
Youtube.
Related stories:
Chinese documentaries expand presence at 2025 Doc Edge
How to pick the right film for you at the Doc Edge Film Festival
Mother of Chooks: Jesse Leaman on his tender chicken documentary
Villarama, who has covered social issues like undocumented migrants in the US and the situation of Filipino workers in Hong Kong, says having the documentary pulled out of Philippine's film festival, just two days before its debut, came as a shock.
“I’m still recovering from that trauma, because it’s the first time for me as an independent filmmaker to encounter that,” Villarama told
Nine to noon
.
“When [the festival’s organisers] informed us that the entire festival is at risk of being cancelled if they don’t pull out the film then that became real. I couldn’t do that to other filmmakers who also had their challenges making the film, it’s not very easy to make films like this. So we decided to agree. It was difficult to process.”
Documentary director Baby Ruth Villarama with the film crew in the Philippines.
Supplied / Elephant Publicity
She says although the organisers didn’t provide additional information about what “external forces” were getting in the way, media reports narrowed it down and “connected the dots”.
The Consulate-General of People’s Republic of China in Auckland had asked Doc Edge to refrain from screening the documentary, claiming the film was “rife with disinformation and false propaganda to serve as (a) political tool for the Philippines”.
Earlier this month,
Doc Edge declined the request
, saying it was happy to publicise the view of the Chinese Consulate-General for the sake of transparency and fairness but it stood by its
kaupapa
of independence and curatorial freedom.
“We encourage audiences to seek their own sources, view the film, and engage in open conversation and dialogue.”
Villarama says she’s grateful that Doc Edge did not bow down to pressure.
“They took that firm decision, that principled decision to keep the film in the festival. They can always remove my film and go on … but they stood behind a small film from the Philippines and that means so much.”
She says they were not supported nor funded by the government whilst following the fishermen for 60 days to make the documentary and only asked for permission to access the Coastguard ship for filming purposes.
“Until now, we’re still paying some of the debts from our production work but it’s okay, it’s part of it, it’s part of the adventure and it’s worth every hassle and challenge.”
She says it is important for storytellers like her to represent the unheard voice of the fishermen involved in the Rotation and Reprovision (RORE) missions – a military operation that delivers food and aid to the soldiers posted in remote areas “to guard the Philippines, to guard our sovereignty”.
“Because of the [escalating] situation, it’s getting harder and harder to deliver food to our soldiers there. Even the fisher folk, with their way of life of fishing, it’s also a challenge for them to harvest their fish because of this external encroachment.”
The missions are done in stealth and without being detected, “like a ninja”, Villarama says. But she was most emotionally struck by what the fishermen had to put with, she says.
“It breaks our heart to realise the challenges they have to face and the bullying they have to endure to make sure their ends meet and to make sure there’s fish for everyone to eat. Like the tuna that we deliver to hotels and restaurants and even export in other countries. That’s the effort that comes from the hand of our fisherfolk.”
Observing the “divine” beauty of the islands and sea, she felt humans needed to do better to protect and share the resources nature was giving us for free.

data.title: Astronomers race to study interstellar interloper
data.author: bikenaga
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕3I/ATLAS等星际天体的观测与探测技术的讨论

不同观点：
• **[ddahlen]** 作为一名轨道动力学博士生，他提到当前很多天文学家正在申请望远镜的自由支配时间，以观测3I/ATLAS。由于该天体即将运行到太阳另一侧，目前的观测窗口有限。同时，它接近银河平面，背景恒星众多，观测难度增加。他还分享了一个开源的计算工具用于小行星和彗星的轨道计算。

• **[rtkwe]** 提到了“Project Lyra”计划，这是一个针对星际天体（如ʻOumuamua或2I/Borisov）的理论飞越任务。该计划的轨迹设计非常复杂，例如2030年发射并在2052年飞越，借助木星和靠近太阳的重力辅助。然而，由于资金问题，这样的任务能否实现仍存在疑问。

• **[layer8]** 提供了有关3I/ATLAS轨迹的可视化资源，包括维基百科上的动画和3D互动查看器，帮助其他讨论者更直观地理解该天体的运动。

• **[csours]** 提出在物理拦截星际天体非常困难的情况下，其他可能的替代方案，例如激光、Masers、彗尾取样或预先部署拦截器。他还提到即将上线的Vera Rubin望远镜可能会发现更多此类天体。

• **[TheBlight]** 同意Vera Rubin望远镜将带来大量星际天体探测数据，但指出目前尚未开始提供数据。

• **[GMoromisato]** 强调3I是第三个发现的星际天体，并认为我们正处于发现星际天体新群体的开端，类似于19世纪初发现小行星带的过程。他还提出未来十年可能发现更多此类天体。

• **[rbanffy]** 好奇需要什么样的火箭才能发射预包装的探测器拦截这些天体，并提出是否可以用SLS搭载立方体卫星。

补充讨论：
• **[k__]** 幽默地提到希望结局不会像游戏《Outer Wilds》那样。
• **[xoxxala]** 分享了一个关于3I/ATLAS的Sixty Symbols视频 overview。
• **[Eduard]** 提供了一个存档链接，未具体说明内容。
• **[skc]** 对天体移动速度表示惊叹。
• **[pfdietz]** 确认该天体的双曲线过剩，表明它确实不是太阳系天体。
• **[cryptonector]** 提到了《Rama》小说中的内容，暗指可能存在类似星际物体的科幻情节。

争议焦点：
• 目前讨论中未见明显争议，但有对星际天体拦截任务的可行性和未来发现的预期存在不同看法，尤其是Project Lyra任务的实际可行性与Vera Rubin望远镜上线后的数据影响。

data.title: Riverside issues citations for illegal fireworks spotted by police drones
data.author: bikenaga
data.article_summary: 在第四 of July 假期周末，河滨市使用无人机抓捕非法燃放烟花者，并开出了数十张罚单。警方在节日前夕部署了五架无人机巡查，重点打击非法烟花，特别是来自外州或外国的高度危险的迫击炮类烟花。每张罚单为1500美元，针对每24小时内的违规行为进行罚款。警方通过无人机视频证据确认了60名房产所有者，并将罚款与房产挂钩。尽管一些居民认为这种方式不公平，警方发言人则表示，这与使用直升机巡逻无异，所有罚单都有明确的视频证据支持。被罚者有权上诉。

• 一些用户（如评论中的Chris1407和AztecCenturion）对BluOS的软件更新持负面态度。他们认为更新后出现了功能退步，比如更新导致原有功能的失效（如播放列表管理问题）以及系统稳定性的下降（如频繁崩溃）。这些用户对厂商的更新策略表示不满，认为更新没有带来实质性的改进，反而引入了新的问题。

• 另一部分用户（如Kernow1967）则持相对中立的立场，认为虽然更新后确实出现了一些问题，但整体上系统依然能正常工作，只是某些小问题影响了体验。这类用户虽然对更新有一定不满，但仍在观望厂商是否会迅速修复问题。

• 还有用户（如Jb1971）对更新持正面态度，认为BluOS的更新总体上是有益的，特别是在界面和性能上有改进，并认为部分问题可能是由于个体设备或配置差异导致的，而不是更新本身的普遍问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点集中在软件更新的质量和厂商的反馈机制上。负面观点的用户批评厂商没有及时修复问题或对用户反馈不够重视。

• 一些用户提到对更新后出现的新功能的认可，但也强调这些功能不应以牺牲系统稳定性为代价。

• 讨论中还涉及对竞争产品（如Sonos）的比较，部分用户认为其他品牌在软件更新和稳定性方面表现更好，这可能是用户考虑转向其他品牌的原因。

• 总体来看，用户对BluOS的更新体验存在明显分歧，部分用户因实际遇到的问题而感到失望，而另一些用户则能接受或尚未遇到严重问题。

Riverside issues citations for illegal fireworks spotted by drones over Fourth of July weekend
Riverside issues citations for illegal fireworks spotted by drones over Fourth of July weekend
02:39
The city of Riverside has issued dozens of citations for the use of illegal fireworks that were spotted by police drones patrolling the skies over the Fourth of July holiday weekend.
Beginning in the days leading up to the holiday, Riverside police launched five different drones to start looking for firework activity, part of their new plan to catch people partaking in the illegal pyrotechnics.
"We're talking about the very illegal explosive mortars. The ones that are illegal in the state of California," said Riverside Police Department Spokesperson Officer Ryan Railsback. "You have to bring those from outside the state, or outside the country. ... This is dangerous for them to do. That's why our city has taken this stance of saying it's not allowed and putting a hefty fine attached to it."
He says that it wasn't very hard to find people who were breaking the law, and letters with fines were sent out this week. Each fine is $1,500 and people can be fined for violations every 24 hours, Railsback said.
"There's no disputing what you're gonna see on the video. The fireworks that were going off are affiliated with your property, it's plain as day on this video," he said.
Related:
Riverside County begins annual crackdown on illegal fireworks
Police say that the letters will contain what they call administrative citations. They aren't criminal and the fine is placed against the property for using fireworks. Those who wish to appeal may do so, Railsback said.
"They have every right to appeal it, but we feel every citation going out has a very strong video evidence to support it," he said.
So far, Railsback says that 60 property owners have been identified to be receiving fines.
Some residents said that the way police were going about issuing citations isn't fair.
"I think it's wrong," said one Riverside man. "I mean, if you're gonna city somebody do it person to person. That's an invasion of property."
Railsback said it's no different than law enforcement departments utilizing helicopters.
"We're in a rightful place in the sky. It's no different than when we have our police helicopter, we have two brand new, or newer helicopters that go patrol looking for things, helping support the officers on the ground," he said.

data.title: Edward Burtynsky's monumental chronicle of the human impact on the planet
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍加拿大摄影师爱德华·伯汀斯基（Edward Burtynsky）的摄影作品，他记录了地球在过去四十年中因人口增长和经济扩张带来的巨大变化。伯汀斯基通过航拍和大视角展示人类活动对自然景观的影响，如矿山、采石场、农业和工业等场景。他的作品强调了人类对地球资源的过度开发，如在刚果民主共和国的矿场和中国的快速城市化进程。伯汀斯基的摄影不仅展示了宏大的场景，还通过细致的观察揭示了这些变化背后的人类活动及其对环境的深远影响。他的作品与已故摄影师塞巴斯蒂昂·萨尔加多（Sebastião Salgado）的人文视角形成互补，共同记录了人类加速发展对地球的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于Edward Burtynsky作品《Manufactured Landscapes》的评价及其反映的人类发展对环境的影响]

不同观点：
• [支持欣赏Burtynsky的作品] cardamomo推荐了纪录片《Manufactured Landscapes》，认为它非常出色，并建议至少观看开头部分，显示出对Burtynsky作品的赞赏和推荐态度。

• [对作品感到悲哀] jebarker提到阅读《The Sixth Extinction》后，对Burtynsky照片中展示的快速人类发展感到悲哀。尽管承认经济利益，但更关注其对地球环境的可怕影响，表现出对环境破坏的忧虑。

• [提供额外资源] pseudolus提供了Burtynsky在纽约国际摄影中心的展览链接以及一篇包含更多照片和评论的文章，为讨论提供了更多参考资料。

• [将作品与流行文化对比] AndrewKemendo将Burtynsky的作品与电影《WALL-E》和《蠢蛋进化论》中的世界进行比较，暗示这些作品中反映的反乌托邦景象与Burtynsky的作品有相似之处，带有批评现代社会发展方向的意味。

• [讽刺评论] atoav以讽刺的口吻提到第一张照片一定是破坏景观的风车，暗示对某些人认为风力发电等绿色能源也会破坏景观的看法的不满或不认同。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Burtynsky作品所展示的大规模工业和经济发展对环境的巨大影响，以及这些影响是否可以通过经济利益来合理化。
• 不同评论者对作品的情感反应各异，有的赞赏其艺术价值，有的则对其反映的环境问题感到悲哀。
• 讨论还涉及对绿色能源的看法，atoav的评论暗示了对某些环境保护者批评风力发电的讽刺。

44547089.article_content:
Save this story
Save this story
Save this story
Save this story
Since Edward Burtynsky’s birth in Ontario, Canada, in 1955, the Earth’s population has roughly tripled, and its economy has grown tenfold. This “great acceleration,” to use the title of the (exquisitely curated and hung) retrospective newly installed at the International Center of Photography, on the Lower East Side, is the most anomalous stretch in human history, and during the past four decades Burtynsky has been almost certainly its greatest visual chronicler—a poet of scale, making use of ever-better lenses and innovations such as drones to gain an ever more encompassing perspective. Perhaps the only photographer to have backed up farther from this subject was Bill Anders, the Apollo 8 astronaut who gave us “
Earthrise
,” in 1968. But that image was taken from too far away to even hint at the stress that the Earth was undergoing as the human footprint expanded. Burtynsky had the perfect depth of field for the task, and his images have become steadily more complicated over time.
“Homesteads #29,” Walkerville, Montana, U.S.A., 1985.
“Dryland Farming #27,” Monegros County, Aragon, Spain, 2010.
Consider, for instance, “Mines #23,” a study of a copper pit in Utah, from 1983. Already the sense of geological proportion is emergent; it takes a moment to orient yourself and understand that the tiny trucks in the middle of the scene are actually gargantuan earthmovers. Or “Quarry #1,” a 2016 study of the Italian mountainsides where Carrara marble is extracted—it’s a masterpiece of geometry and brooding color that reminds me of Bruegel’s great “Tower of Babel.” But it’s “Dry Tailings #1,” from another copper mine, this one in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which really establishes the dilemma of our age. At first, it seems to be a study in hue—the ochres, tawnies, pinks, and roses that the mineral-rich soil produces. But, if you look closely, you can see minuscule human figures that both reveal the scale and illuminate the drama—these figures are emerging after hours, to illicitly comb through the tailings in search of small chunks of
the cobalt that helps power cell-phone batteries
. Perhaps it will remind you, as it did me, of
Sebastião Salgado
’s indelible images of Brazilian gold miners climbing the sides of a pit, from the nineteen-eighties. Salgado, who, until his death in May was a close friend of Burtynsky’s, focussed quite literally on the human cost of the acceleration; Burtynsky’s concentration on the landscapes being ravaged makes their combined works an irreplaceable diptych.
“Dry Tailings #1,” Kolwezi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2024.
It’s not that Burtynsky can’t photograph bodies and faces—tender portraits, such as “Shipbreaking #14,” part of his series on the almost unbelievable story of the Bangladeshi men who dismantled retired oil tankers by hand, show that he connects quite easily on the smaller scale with people in his vast world. But it’s the vastness that’s his true subject.
“Shipbreaking #14,” Chittagong, Bangladesh, 2000.
Look at his account of agriculture and farming, which has altered more of the Earth’s surface than any other activity. There’s almost never a farmer in sight—instead, it’s the sheer size of the industrial enterprise that draws his eye. The largest print in the show, at twenty-eight feet by twenty-eight feet, is titled “Pivot Irrigation #8,” and was taken from a helicopter hovering thirty-five hundred feet above the high plains of Texas. Framed almost formally by perfectly squared-off farm roads, it shows the giant circle of fertility that comes from sprinklers drawing on the (depleting) Ogallala Aquifer beneath; the detail is so fine that you can stare at it for an hour, constantly noticing new details (combine tracks turning at the edge of the irrigated circle, say).
“Pivot Irrigation #8,” High Plains, Texas Panhandle, U.S.A., 2012.
In other images, people are present but rendered almost as parts of the great machine that powers the acceleration. “Manufacturing #10b,” shot in 2005 in Xiamen City, captures, like no picture I have ever seen, China’s extraordinary economic surge as the millennium began. The ranks of yellow-clad workers disappearing into an almost infinite distance are all assembling drip coffeemakers.
China’s relentless rush is captured in other images, perhaps most powerfully in “Feng Jie #4,” which shows workers in 2002 racing to disassemble the city where they lived before it would be drowned by
the Three Gorges Dam
, which has the greatest generating capacity of any dam in the world. What at first seems to be undifferentiated rubble are actually piles of bricks, carefully numbered so that their owners can be compensated; in the background, a roving troop of boys follow leaders hoisting brightly colored flags as they scavenge for wood that might someday float up and damage the turbines; their bonfires brush smoke across this battlefield scene.
“Manufacturing #10b,” Cankun Fact

data.title: Nuclear Explosion for Carbon Sequestration
data.author: energy123
data.article_summary: 文章提出利用海底核爆炸加速玄武岩风化，从而实现大规模碳捕集，以应对气候变化。通过精确控制海底核爆位置，可限制 debris、辐射和能量扩散，同时促进岩石风化，有效捕捉大气中的二氧化碳。研究分析了所需的爆炸参数以确保高效碳捕集和最小副作用，强调爆炸当量需达到数十亿吨以产生全球气候影响。尽管方案激进，文章通过安全性、生态保护、政治和经济可行性等方面论证其可行性，提出将核技术作为减碳手段的新视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用核爆炸进行碳封存的可行性与风险

不同观点：
• Perihelions认为该论文缺乏技术分析，质疑是否有更好的来源来进行这一讨论，暗示对该论文的可靠性存疑。
• Freeslave提出是否可以通过多次较小规模的核爆炸来达到与一次大规模爆炸（81百万吨）相同的效果，质疑实现方式的可行性。
• Duanemclemore引用Wes Anderson的风格幽默地指出，论文假设了“犁头计划”执行得不够彻底，表示在完全阅读论文前保持判断，但认为这个讨论很有趣。
• John7878781担心在海底引爆核弹可能会释放已经封存的碳，认为这个想法不够周全，存在潜在风险。
• LargoLasskhyfv以幽默方式回应，未提出具体观点。
• Schobi认为没有单一的解决方案，不能仅依靠建造价值100亿美元的核弹计划来解决问题，强调需要综合运用多种手段来摆脱化石燃料，并认为越早开始越好。
• Biohcacker84认为越来越多人发明高风险的碳封存方法，而忽视了简单、低风险的措施，如将生物炭添加到农田作为农业补贴，或者通过增加海洋生物量来封存碳，质疑使用核弹进行碳封存的合理性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种碳封存方法的比较，包括生物炭添加、海洋施肥等，与使用核爆炸的对比。
• 争议的焦点在于使用核爆炸进行碳封存的风险与可行性，以及是否存在更安全、有效的替代方案。
• 幽默和讽刺（如"Nukewards Ho!"）在讨论中也起到了一定的调节作用，但并未对核心议题提出具体见解。

Title:
Nuclear Explosions for Large Scale Carbon Sequestration
Authors:
Andrew Haverly
View a PDF of the paper titled Nuclear Explosions for Large Scale Carbon Sequestration, by Andrew Haverly
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Confronting the escalating threat of climate change requires innovative and large-scale interventions. This paper presents a bold proposal to employ a buried nuclear explosion in a remote basaltic seabed for pulverizing basalt, thereby accelerating carbon sequestration through Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW). By precisely locating the explosion beneath the seabed, we aim to confine debris, radiation, and energy while ensuring rapid rock weathering at a scale substantial enough to make a meaningful dent in atmospheric carbon levels. Our analysis outlines the parameters essential for efficient carbon capture and minimal collateral effects, emphasizing that a yield on the order of gigatons is critical for global climate impact. Although this approach may appear radical, we illustrate its feasibility by examining safety factors, preservation of local ecosystems, political considerations, and financial viability. This work argues for reimagining nuclear technology not merely as a destructive force but as a potential catalyst for decarbonization, thereby inviting further exploration of pioneering solutions in the fight against climate change.

• Duanemclemore引用Wes Anderson的风格幽默地指出，论文假设了“犁头计划”执行得不够彻底，表示在完全阅读论文前保持判断，但认为这个讨论很有趣。
• John7878781担心在海底引爆核弹可能会释放已经封存的碳，认为这个想法不够周全，存在潜在风险。
• LargoLasskhyfv以幽默方式回应，未提出具体观点。
• Schobi认为没有单一的解决方案，不能仅依靠建造价值100亿美元的核弹计划来解决问题，强调需要综合运用多种手段来摆脱化石燃料，并认为越早开始越好。
• Biohcacker84认为越来越多人发明高风险的碳封存方法，而忽视了简单、低风险的措施，如将生物炭添加到农田作为农业补贴，或者通过增加海洋生物量来封存碳，质疑使用核弹进行碳封存的合理性。

• 讨论中涉及了多种碳封存方法的比较，包括生物炭添加、海洋施肥等，与使用核爆炸的对比。
• 争议的焦点在于使用核爆炸进行碳封存的风险与可行性，以及是否存在更安全、有效的替代方案。
• 幽默和讽刺（如"Nukewards Ho!"）在讨论中也起到了一定的调节作用，但并未对核心议题提出具体见解。

data.title: Experimental imperative-style music sequence generator engine
data.author: bwidlar
data.article_summary: **pattrns** 是一个实验性的命令式音乐序列生成引擎，支持通过 Rust 库（静态、编译型）或 Lua 脚本引擎（动态、解释型）以编程方式创建音乐序列，适合用于现场编码音乐。它通过节奏（脉冲生成器）、门限（脉冲过滤器）和发射器（音符或参数事件生成器）三个组件生成音乐序列，分离节奏和音调部分以便自由组合。文档和指南可通过本地生成，提供 Rust 和 Lua 的示例。该引擎不生成音频，需结合支持 pattrns 的应用使用。项目基于 AGPL-3.0 许可证发布。

pattrns
pattrns
is an experimental imperative-style music sequence generator engine.
It allows you to programmatically create music sequences either in plain
Rust
as library (
static, compiled
) or in
Lua
as a scripting engine (
dynamic, interpreted
). So it's also suitable for
live coding music
.
In addition to its imperative event generator approach, it also supports the creation of musical events using
tidalcycle
's mini-notation.
This crate only deals with the
generation of raw musical events
. It does not generate audio. You must use an application with built-in support for pattrns to use it.
Conceptional Overview
pattrns generates musical sequences using three distinct components, stages:
Rhythm
: (
pulse
in scripts) dynamic pulse generator to define a rhythmical pulse train.
Gate
: (
gate
in scripts) optional pulse filter between rhythm and event emitter.
Emitter
: (
event
in scripts), dynamic note or parameter event generator which gets triggered by the pulse train.
By separating the rhythmical from the tonal part of a musical sequence, each part can be freely modified, composed and (re)combined as it fits.
Documentation & Guides
Read the
Scripting Book
.
It contains an introduction, guides, full Lua API documentation and bunch of script examples.
The Rust backend uses standard Rust documentation features. The docs are currently not hosted online (yet), but you can generate them locally via
cargo doc --open
.
Applications
Online Playground
is a simple browser based playground app. It allows you to learn and test how pattrns works.
Renoise
uses pattrns in its
phrase editor
.
Integration Examples
examples/play.rs
demonstrates how to use patterns using only Rust: it defines and plays a little music thing. The content can only be changed at compile time.
examples/play-script.rs
is an example using the Lua API: it also defines and plays a little music thing, but its content can be added/removed and changed on the fly to do some basic live music hacking.
Acknowledgements
Thanks to
unlessgames
for adding the Tidal Cycles mini-notation support.
Contribute
Patches are welcome! Please fork the latest git repository and create a feature or bugfix branch.
Licence
pattrns is distributed under the terms of the
GNU Affero General Public License V3
.

data.title: Programming Affordances That Invite Mistakes
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程中的错误处理设计和实践

不同观点：
• mb20281认为错误处理不足是主要问题，指出在发送邮件之前应先保存到数据库，以确保数据一致性。这种顺序问题会导致不可靠的结果。
• BoppreH指出`or die()`并不是一种好的设计选择，而是一种常见的习惯用法。同时提到类似`file_exists(path)`和`db.query(string)`等函数可能会引发难以调试的竞争条件和SQL注入问题。
• wongarsu则认为PHP的“忽略错误继续运行”的哲学导致了开发者习惯性地使用`or die()`，而在某些情况下，继续运行可能才是正确的行为。并质疑如果编程语言默认会崩溃（如Java的异常机制），开发者是否会更注重错误处理。
• sgtpeppr强调了使正确的事情容易做、错误的事情难以做的重要性，并提到一些开发者习惯于用“这是我们一直以来的做法”来为不好的设计选择辩护，导致问题难以解决。
• hnthrow90348765认为这是一个设计和需求问题，而非语言问题。指出如果没有明确的规划和需求说明，开发者很难考虑到所有可能的错误情况，尤其是在高风险场景下。
• anonzzzies对比了PHP和Node.js中的错误处理，指出`die()`只影响当前请求，而`process.exit()`会退出整个Node服务器。同时提到在实际项目中，常见到不完整的错误处理代码，并建议使用工具检测未处理的情况以提高安全性。
• jauco提供了一个外部资源，Joe Duffy的一篇文章，区分了不同种类的错误以及编程语言应如何处理它们。
• hyperhello指出即便错误处理设计不当，测试不足也是问题，认为至少应该有一次测试能发现失败。
• golergka提到“Pit of Success”（成功之坑）概念，强调设计应使得开发者自然而然地做出正确的选择。

补充讨论：
• 错误处理的设计不仅涉及编程语言的特性，还包括开发者的习惯和项目需求。
• 争议的焦点在于如何在语言设计和开发实践中平衡错误处理的复杂性和实用性。
• 测试和代码审查的重要性在讨论中也被提及，作为发现和纠正错误处理问题的手段。

data.title: Aeron: Efficient reliable UDP unicast, UDP multicast, and IPC message transport
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Aeron是一个高效可靠的 messaging 系统，支持UDP单播、多播以及进程间通信（IPC）。它提供Java、C、C++和.NET客户端，能够在不同机器或同一机器上的进程间高效交换消息。Aeron具备高吞吐量和低延迟特性，集成Simple Binary Encoding (SBE)以提升消息编解码性能。其Archive模块支持将消息流存储到持久存储中，Aeron Cluster则基于Raft算法提供容错服务。Aeron由Adaptive Financial Consulting拥有和运营，提供培训、咨询等服务，并支持一些专有增强功能如内核 bypass 和高速加密。文档和源码可在其GitHub页面和Maven Central获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Aeron的性能和可靠性，以及其使用的UDP和多播技术在实际应用中的表现。

不同观点：
• Veserv认为Aeron的性能并不如宣传的那样高性能。他通过AWS和GCP上的传输协议基准测试数据指出，Aeron在多核心情况下的吞吐量表现不佳，远低于普通的TCP堆栈。他质疑Aeron是否真正达到了高性能的标准，尽管Aeron在延迟和多播支持方面可能有其他优势。

• Vodou基于多年维护使用多播通信的应用套件的经验，对多播的可靠性提出质疑。他认为多播在理论上很好，但在实际应用中由于网络设备和操作系统的问题会带来很多麻烦。他表示不会再在新系统中依赖多播技术。

• Buybackoff认为Aeron的存在本身就是一个重要的贡献，特别是在低延迟系统中。他指出Aeron在单数据中心内的延迟表现优于TCP，尤其是在P99+延迟方面。他还提到Aeron在多播支持上的优势，但也指出在跨数据中心设置中的一些挑战，如缓冲区配置和包丢失问题。

• Neomantra强调Aeron的系统架构和“机械同情”设计理念，认为其高性能不仅仅来自于UDP和多播支持。他详细描述了Aeron的服务器和客户端架构，以及如何通过共享内存队列实现高效的消息传递。

• Arnold_palmur赞赏Aeron代码库的软件质量，认为它是研究软件质量的优秀开源项目，特别是对于Java开发者。

• Readthenotes1对可靠UDP被多次实现的现象表示疑问，暗示可能有重复劳动。

• Fuzzfactor表示喜欢多播的概念，但没有提供具体的使用体验或技术分析。

补充讨论：
• Aeron的性能优势在低延迟和高并发场景下的体现，特别是在单数据中心内，但在跨数据中心时可能不如TCP。
• 多播技术在实际应用中的可靠性问题，特别是在不同网络设备和操作系统上的表现。
• Aeron架构的独特设计及其在共享内存和消息队列方面的创新应用。
• Aeron代码库作为开源项目的质量和学习价值。

争议焦点：
• Aeron在多核心情况下的性能是否真正达到高性能标准，特别是与TCP相比。
• 多播技术的实际可靠性和应用场景的局限性。

Aeron
Efficient reliable UDP unicast, UDP multicast, and IPC message transport. Java, C, and C++ clients are available in this
repository, and a
.NET client
is available. All
clients can exchange messages across machines, or on the same machine via IPC, very efficiently. Message streams can be
recorded by the
Archive
module to persistent storage
for later, or real-time, replay. Aeron
Cluster
provides support for fault-tolerant services as replicated state machines based on the
Raft
consensus algorithm.
Performance is the key focus. A design goal for Aeron is to be the highest throughput with the lowest and most
predictable latency of any messaging system. Aeron integrates with
Simple Binary Encoding (SBE)
for the best possible message
encoding and decoding performance. Many of the data structures used in the creation of Aeron have been factored out to
the
Agrona
project.
For details of usage, protocol specification, FAQ, etc. please check out the
Wiki
.
For the latest version information and changes see the
Change Log
with Java
downloads
at
Maven Central
.
Aeron is owned and operated by Adaptive Financial Consulting. Originally created by Martin Thompson and Todd Montgomery, the Aeron team joined Adaptive in 2022.
For Business users, to get started with Aeron Premium, please visit
Aeron.io
We provide a range of services including:
Training for development and operations with Aeron and Aeron Cluster.
Consulting, for example if you’re not sure how to design your system or need help tuning your system.
We also offer a number of proprietary enhancements on top of Aeron and Aeron Cluster such as kernel bypass (ef_vi, AWS DPDK, and VMA) for increased performance, and blazing fast encryption with ATS.
If you’re building a new trading system, we have experienced Aeron developers who can help.
Please get in touch at
sales@aeron.io
if you would like to learn more about any of these.

44544862.article_summary: Aeron是一个高效可靠的 messaging 系统，支持UDP单播、多播以及进程间通信（IPC）。它提供Java、C、C++和.NET客户端，能够在不同机器或同一机器上的进程间高效交换消息。Aeron具备高吞吐量和低延迟特性，集成Simple Binary Encoding (SBE)以提升消息编解码性能。其Archive模块支持将消息流存储到持久存储中，Aeron Cluster则基于Raft算法提供容错服务。Aeron由Adaptive Financial Consulting拥有和运营，提供培训、咨询等服务，并支持一些专有增强功能如内核 bypass 和高速加密。文档和源码可在其GitHub页面和Maven Central获取。

主要讨论点：Aeron的性能和可靠性，以及其使用的UDP和多播技术在实际应用中的表现。

不同观点：
• Veserv认为Aeron的性能并不如宣传的那样高性能。他通过AWS和GCP上的传输协议基准测试数据指出，Aeron在多核心情况下的吞吐量表现不佳，远低于普通的TCP堆栈。他质疑Aeron是否真正达到了高性能的标准，尽管Aeron在延迟和多播支持方面可能有其他优势。

• Vodou基于多年维护使用多播通信的应用套件的经验，对多播的可靠性提出质疑。他认为多播在理论上很好，但在实际应用中由于网络设备和操作系统的问题会带来很多麻烦。他表示不会再在新系统中依赖多播技术。

• Buybackoff认为Aeron的存在本身就是一个重要的贡献，特别是在低延迟系统中。他指出Aeron在单数据中心内的延迟表现优于TCP，尤其是在P99+延迟方面。他还提到Aeron在多播支持上的优势，但也指出在跨数据中心设置中的一些挑战，如缓冲区配置和包丢失问题。

• Aeron在多核心情况下的性能是否真正达到高性能标准，特别是与TCP相比。
• 多播技术的实际可靠性和应用场景的局限性。

data.title: Parse, Don’t Validate – Some C Safety Tips
data.author: lelanthran
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了“解析而非验证”技术在C语言中的应用，以减少可被利用的错误风险。作者指出，常见的验证方法会导致系统深处的代码重复验证输入，增加错误机会。通过在输入边界处直接解析输入数据为特定类型（如`email_t`），可以避免系统内部重复验证的问题。文章建议使用不透明类型来替代`char *`，确保数据类型安全，防止恶意输入。这种方法不仅提高了安全性，还能借助编译器类型检查进一步减少攻击面。最终，只有边界处的函数处理原始`char *`输入，内部函数只接受已验证的类型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"解析而非验证"（Parse, Don't Validate）编程理念的讨论，涉及数据结构选择、新类型（newtype）的使用、代码可维护性以及在不同语言（尤其是C和Haskell）中的实际应用问题。

不同观点：
• [myaccountonhn] 认为将输入解析为适合问题域的数据结构是好的做法，可以提高代码的可维护性，减少分散的验证检查。但他反对过度使用新类型包装，认为这会增加不必要的仪式性代码（boilerplate），特别是在数据可以合理表示为基本类型的情况下。他还指出，与大量使用新类型的Haskell/Elm库交互时会遇到问题，尤其是在库没有提供访问内部数据的方法时。
• [hackrmn] 支持"解析而非验证"的理念，并强调使用语言的类型系统来处理输入的重要性。他批评了在代码中到处复制验证函数的做法，并指出了在处理URI和日期时间时常见的问题。然而，他提到自己的观点常常不被同事接受，他们更倾向于传统的编码方式。
• [o11c] 讨论了C语言中使用`_t`作为自定义类型后缀的问题，指出这可能会导致与未来标准类型的冲突。他还批评了通过将变量设置为`NULL`来防止双重释放的做法，认为C语言在处理对象所有权方面表现不佳。
• [hansvm] 提出了"解析而非验证"在实际代码库中可能导致类型组合爆炸的问题，指出这会产生大量的中间类型和解析代码。他提出了一种在Zig语言中使用编译时标记来解决此问题的方案。
• [pianoben] 认为虽然"解析而非验证"的理念是好的，但在处理解析结果时会遇到困难，尤其是在需要将自定义类型转换为字符串或其他格式时，可能需要编写大量的辅助函数。
• [anon-3988] 强调在C语言中使用新类型模式来确保安全性的重要性，建议将所有指针操作封装在结构体中，并只在与外部库交互时使用原始指针。

补充讨论：
• [charcircuit] 表示不信任C开发者在字符串解析方面的能力，暗示C语言在这方面的脆弱性。
• [belter] 认为"解析而非验证"模式虽然有帮助，但只是安全防御的一部分，还需要结合资源限制和其他保护措施。
• [jkuli] 幽默地指出二次验证是安全的，并提到在讨论中不应攻击他人。
• [mrkeen] 对示例代码中使用`email_t`和`PARSE_ERROR`的类型设计提出了质疑，认为这种设计不合理，编译时应该报错。

争议焦点：
• 新类型（newtype）的必要性和使用范围：一方认为新类型增加了不必要的复杂性，另一方认为新类型可以提高代码的安全性和清晰度。
• "解析而非验证"在实际应用中的可行性：有人支持其理念，但指出在处理结果时会遇到实际困难，特别是在C语言中。
• C语言中指针操作和类型安全的平衡：讨论中有人指出C语言在处理所有权和类型安全方面的缺陷，并提出了不同的解决方案。

âA good programmer is someone who looks both ways before crossing a one-way street.â â Doug Linder
previous:
Contents
Posted by Lelanthran
2025-03-27
âParse, Donât Validateâ
- the long version
If youâve read the original post on
âParse, Donât Validateâ
you may have noticed that it focuses primarily on conceptual correctness. Here, Iâll build on that by showing how this technique can be used outside of niche academic languages by demonstrating it in a language that is as practical as it is dangerous - C.
In this blog post you will see three techniques of reducing the risk of exploitable errors in C.
âParse, Donât Validateâ
- the TLDR version
The basic idea is this:
Data Comes Into Your System.
Your System Processes It.
Your first instinct, when your system receives as input an email address (for example), is to perform
validateEmail(untrustedInput)
and then pass the validated string further into the depths of the system for usage.
The problem is that other code deep within the rest of the system is going to
also
do some sort of validation on the string they just got. Every single function deep within the bowels of the system will
still
need to validate the input before processing it.
Iâll bet good money that the processing functions will attempt to validate their input. Because theyâre logically far away from the boundary, theyâll either do it a different way or fail to do it altogether.
So instead of this:
// Pseudocode
if
(validateEmail(untrustedInput) != true) {
return
error;
}
// Rest of system uses `untrustedInput`
Rather do this instead:
// Pseudocode
email_t theEmail = parseEmail(untrustedInput);
if
(theEmail == PARSE_ERROR) {
return
error;
}
// Rest of system uses `theEmail`
This removes any opportunity for errors to creep in within the rest of the system, such as some other code using a different
validateEmail
function on the
untrustedInput
, for example.
Some conventions for Safety in C.
What does this have to do with C strings? Good question.
Much to the surprise of, well, everybody, C
actually has
type safety. Sure, it isnât as enforceable as (for example) Rustâ¦ and, sure, if you are willing to do extra work you can bypass it, but, at the end of the day, the compiler
will still warn you
if you try to add a number to a string and assign the result to a function.
With some exceptions, when you mismatch types, the compiler
will
tell you about it.
The problem isnât that C lacks type safety (it clearly enforces most types in most expressions), itâs that raw pointers do not encode semantics (e.g., a
char *
doesnât tell you if itâs an email, a name, or a filename).
This is pretty much the same in every language; if you have a function
store_user()
which accepts two strings, an email and a user name, then no type safety in the world is going to save you if you accidentally swap the arguments around when calling the function.
But, you still have options â even in C â by creating new string types; one for email and another for user name.
When writing in C, instead of passing
char *
around as strings, or (safer, but not by much) using an existing string library that stores length + bufferâ¦ rather create an opaque type for it.
You parse the input into the correct type
once
, and then functions which accept that type will produce a compile error if you mix things up.
To create opaque types,
read this post
.
When you create the correct types for
data entering the system
, you can then do this:
// C code, not pseudocode
email_t *email = parse_email(untrusted_input);
if
(!email) {
// Handle error
}
In addition to the safey from using opaque types thereâs even more levels of safety here too, starting with:
You remove all occurrences of
char *
values in your system. You force the only occurrences of
char *
values to be at the boundary of your system, where
all input is untrusted anyway!
This is not only for
char *
types though; you can do it to
all
values entering your system.You parse them once into the correct data type, and then code deep in the belly of the system
cannot
be compromised with malicious input, because the
only
data that the rest of the system will see is data that has been parsed into specific types.
When your functions never accept
char *
parameters your risk of pwnage is reduced. By leveraging the typing guarantees in C, you can ensure that the system wonât compile
even if
some heretic decides that they want to pass a
char *
to a function expecting an
email_t
.
Only the functions on the boundary of the system, interfacing to the outside world, should parse input. Everything else should accept
only
type-checkable parameters.
That alone is a big reason to use this approach, but Iâll point out two more opportunities to reduce the attack surface of your system using an actual compilable example consisting of separate compilation units. The untrusted input
email
and
name
come from outside the system.

data.title: New Windows 11 build adds self-healing "quick machine recovery" feature
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 微软正在为Windows 11添加一项名为快速机器恢复（QMR）的新功能，以帮助修复崩溃的电脑。QMR允许电脑启动进入Windows恢复环境（WinRE），连接互联网并下载微软提供的修复程序，解决可能导致电脑无法正常启动的问题。这一技术是微软"Windows弹性计划"的一部分，旨在避免类似2024年中CrowdStrike安全产品更新导致的大规模Windows电脑故障。QMR最初在Windows Insider项目的Canary通道中推出，并可能逐步推广到更广泛的用户群。此外，微软还在准备Windows 11 25H2年度更新，其中一些功能将预先安装但暂时禁用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows 11操作系统的问题与新功能（自修复工具）的讨论

不同观点：
• [anon7000]: 认为Win11是最近几年用过的最不可靠的操作系统，存在卡顿、蓝屏、设备兼容性问题（如音频接口）等，对新推出的自修复工具持怀疑态度，认为Windows的故障排查机制不够透明，且修复工具可能无效。
• [ChocolateGod]: 对微软放弃Windows 10X表示遗憾，认为其可以解决系统升级导致的致命问题，而现在则是在用“权宜之计”应对糟糕的系统设计，类似于Android的更新机制。
• [ksec]: 对Win11的总体评价较为正面，认为虽然仍有一些小问题（如广告和UI），但相比Win10有所改进。希望微软能够更快速地迭代版本，并认为Windows仍有改进空间。
• [potato-peeler]: 对微软Canary测试通道的命名习惯提出质疑，指出与公司内部使用的定义不一致，Canary在其公司是介于开发和测试之间的阶段。
• [instagib]: 提到最近的一次更新导致硬盘无法启动或挂载，新的Win11安装缺少恢复模式，需要手动修复，对系统的稳定性表示担忧。
• [bni]: 批评Windows UI越来越破碎和臃肿，希望微软能够首先解决这些问题。

Microsoft is adding a new recovery mode to Windows to help revive crashing PCs. Called quick machine recovery (QMR), this technology enables Windows 11 PCs to boot into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE, also used by Windows install media and IT shops for various recovery and diagnostic purposes), connect to the Internet, and download Microsoft-provided fixes for "widespread boot issues" that could be keeping the PC from booting properly.
Initially
announced in late 2024
as part of the "Windows Resiliency Initiative," QMR is one of a couple of steps that Microsoft is taking
to prevent a repeat of mid-2024's CrowdStrike outage
, when a bugged update to one of CrowdStrike's security products brought down millions of Windows PCs and servers and caused widespread service outages in many industries. Fixing some of those PCs required booting and fixing each one individually; QMR should make it possible to apply that kind of fix remotely even if a PC is so broken that it can't boot into Windows proper.
The initial version of the QMR feature is
rolling out to Windows 11 PCs
enrolled in the Canary channel of Microsoft's Windows Insider testing program. This is the least stable and most experimental of the four Windows 11 testing channels. As Microsoft adds features and fixes bugs, it should gradually move to the Dev, Beta, and Release Preview channels before rolling out to the Windows user base more broadly.
Preview build 27898 also includes a features that will shrink Taskbar items if you've got too many pins or running apps for everything to fit at once, changes the pop-up that apps use to ask for access to things like the system webcam or microphone, and allows you to add words to the dictionary used for the speech-to-text voice access features, among a handful of other changes.
It's hard to predict when any given Windows Insider feature will roll out to the regular non-preview versions of Windows, but we're likely just a few months out from the launch of Windows 11 25H2, this year's "annual feature update." Some of these updates, like last year's 24H2, are fairly major overhauls that make lots of under-the-hood changes. Others, like 2023's 23H2, mostly exist to change the version number and reset Microsoft's security update clock, as each yearly update is only promised new security updates
for two years after release
.
The 25H2 update looks like one of the relatively minor ones. Microsoft
says
that the two versions "use a shared servicing branch," and that 25H2 features will be "staged" on PCs running Windows 11 24H2, meaning that the code will be installed on systems via Windows Update but that they'll be disabled initially. Installing the 25H2 "update" when it's available will merely enable features that were installed but dormant.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对生产力、工资和企业竞争的影响

不同观点：
• **[aisikaakaccc]**：AI工具提高了开发者的生产力，但产生了一些质量问题。举例说明了高级开发者和低绩效开发者如何使用AI工具，前者虽然产出更多，但质量不佳，而后者则让代码审查过程更加耗时。他认为AI工具在实际使用中并没有网上声称的那么神奇，只有在特定场景（如翻译）中才能显著提高生产力。

• **[jostylr]**：AI带来的生产力提升可能会通过市场竞争影响工资和利润。如果工人能够利用AI工具提高自身竞争力并跳槽到更高薪的岗位，他们的工资可能会提高。此外，企业可以通过降低成本和提高效率来增加利润。最终，AI工具可能会催生更多独立项目和创业机会。

• **[matt_s]**：工人不会从生产力提升中直接受益，因为利润主要流向企业主和管理层。即使AI工具提高了工人的生产力，工人也很难获得相应的工资增长。工人要获得更多收益，可能需要自己创业，但这比单纯编写软件要复杂得多。

• **[grafmax]**：生产力提升通常不会自动转化为工人工资的增加，因为企业主不会主动分享利润，除非受到外部压力。历史数据显示，自1980年以来，生产力与工资之间的差距越来越大，工人的生产力收益大部分流向了富裕阶层。要改变这种情况，可能需要通过工会化等手段对企业主施加压力。

• **[muzani]**：AI工具显著降低了创业和开发的风险与成本，例如快速构建原型和减少技术债务。尽管存在一些失败案例，但总体上AI工具提高了生产力和创业成功率。

• **[molteanu]**：在其公司中，尽管广泛使用AI工具，但并未显著提升开发速度或激发更多创意。AI工具的引入更像是一个没有明确指导的开放选择，缺乏对好坏的判断。

• **[AznHisoka]**：如果所有人都能使用相同的AI工具，那么个别工程师很难通过这些工具获得超常的职业发展或财富积累，因为大家的生产力都得到了提升。

• **[gavinray]**：有些公司正在尝试通过量化和补偿提高生产力的员工来留住他们。虽然这种方法不一定适用于所有组织，但在某些情况下是可行的。

• **[francisofascii]**：AI工具的普及可能导致工程师供过于求，从而降低他们的市场工资。例如，微软的股票价格上涨并没有直接提高工程师的工资。

• **[i_have_an_idea]**：AI工具在特定情况下非常有用，例如挽救和管理不善的外包项目，避免公司遭受重大损失。

• **[mojomark]**：尽管个人日常使用ChatGPT提高效率，但这些提升并未被广泛认可或转化为实际利润。

• **[lifestyleguru]**：尽管AI工具被大肆宣传，但目前尚未看到显著改变生活的软件产品。

• **[metalman]**：AI和NFT等新技术带来了前所未有的利润机会，例如NVIDIA的AI相关产品。

• **[ivape]**：GPT 3.5发布至今不到三年，我们仍在探索其潜在应用，现在判断其长期影响为时尚早。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：AI工具是否真正提升了工人的工资和职业发展。一部分人认为生产力提升不会自动转化为工资增长，而另一部分人则认为通过市场竞争和创业机会可以实现工资增长。
- **实际案例**：评论中提供了多个实际案例，说明AI工具在不同情境下的应用效果，包括提高生产力、降低成本和挽救项目等。
- **历史数据**：引用自1980年以来的生产力与工资差距数据，支持了对生产力收益分配不均的观点。
- **未来展望**：一些评论认为AI工具的潜力尚未完全实现，需要更多时间来观察其长期影响。
